1 Kings (Regum)

[He] led their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and they followed alien gods and worshipped them; therefore the Lord brought upon them all this evil. And it came to pass, at the end of twenty years, after Solomon had built the two houses, that is, the house of the Lord and the house of the king — Hiram king of Tyre providing Solomon with cedar and fir timber and gold according to all his need — then Solomon gave Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee. And Hiram went out from Tyre to see the cities which Solomon had given him, and they did not please him. And he said, "What cities are these that you have given me, my brother?" And he called them the land of Cabul unto this day. And Hiram sent to King Solomon a hundred and twenty talents of gold. This is the sum of the tributes which Solomon offered for building the house of the Lord and his own house, and Millo, and the wall of Jerusalem, and Hazor and Megiddo and Gezer. Pharaoh king of Egypt went up and took Gezer, and burned it with fire, and slew the Canaanites who dwelt in the city, and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon's wife. So Solomon built Gezer, and lower Bethhoron, and Baalath, and Tadmor in the wilderness, in the land, and all the storage towns that belonged to him, and the towns for his chariots, and the towns for his horsemen, and whatsoever pleased him to build in Jerusalem and in Lebanon and in all the land of his dominion. All the people that remained of the Amorites and Hittites and Perizzites and Hivites and Jebusites, who were not of the children of Israel — their descendants who remained in the land, whom the children of Israel had not been able to destroy, these Solomon made bondservants unto this day. But of the children of Israel Solomon made no one a slave; but they were men of war, and his ministers, and his princes, and his captains, and overseers of his chariots and horses. And these were the chiefs set over all the works of Solomon, five hundred and fifty, who had the people subject to them and directed the appointed works. And Pharaoh's daughter went up from the city of David to her house which Solomon had built for her. Then he built Millo. And Solomon offered three times a year burnt offerings and peace offerings upon the altar which he had built to the Lord, and burned incense before the Lord. So the temple was finished. King Solomon also made a fleet at Ezion-geber, which is beside Eloth on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom. And Hiram sent in that fleet his servants, seamen and men who knew the sea, along with the servants of Solomon; and when they had come to Ophir, they took from there four hundred and twenty talents of gold and brought them to King Solomon. [Chapter 10.]

And the queen of Sheba, having heard of the fame of Solomon in the name of the Lord, came to test him with hard questions. And she entered Jerusalem with a very great company and riches, camels bearing spices and very much gold and precious stones, and came to King Solomon, and spoke to him all that was in her heart. And Solomon explained to her all the matters she asked about; there was no matter hidden from the king that he could not answer her. And when the queen of Sheba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house he had built, and the food of his table, and the seating of his servants, and the order of his ministers and their apparel, and his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he offered in the house of the Lord, there was no more spirit left in her; and she said to the king, "The report I heard in my own land of your deeds and your wisdom was true; and I did not believe the reports until I came and saw with my own eyes. And I find that not even half was told me..."

results.translation: The Lord said to the children of Israel: You shall not go in unto them, neither shall any of them come in unto yours; for they will most certainly turn away your hearts to follow their gods. Solomon was joined to these with a most ardent love. And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his women turned away his heart. And when he was now old, his heart was corrupted by his women, to follow strange gods; and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father: but Solomon worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the idol of the Ammonites. And Solomon did that which was not pleasing before the Lord, and did not fully follow the Lord as David his father did. Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh, the idol of Moab, in the mountain that is over against Jerusalem, and for Molech, the idol of the children of Ammon. And in this manner he did for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their gods. Therefore the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned away from the Lord God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice, and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not follow strange gods; and he did not keep what the Lord commanded him. Therefore the Lord said to Solomon: Because you have done this, and have not kept my covenant and my precepts which I commanded you, I will surely rend the kingdom from you, and will give it to your servant. Nevertheless in your days I will not do it for David your father's sake; but I will rend it out of the hand of your son. However I will not take away the whole kingdom; I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant, and for Jerusalem which I have chosen. And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of the royal seed, who was in Edom. For when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the army had gone up to bury those who had been slain, and had killed every male in Edom (for Joab remained there six months with all Israel, until he had destroyed every male in Edom), Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father's servants with him, that he might go into Egypt; Hadad being then a little child. And when they had risen up out of Midian, they came to Paran; and they took men with them out of Paran, and came into Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house, and appointed him food, and assigned him land. And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen. And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, and Tahpenes brought him up in the house of Pharaoh; and Genubath dwelt with Pharaoh's household among the sons of Pharaoh. And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David had slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the army was dead, he said to Pharaoh: Let me depart, that I may go to my own country. And Pharaoh said to him: What do you lack with me, that you seek to go to your own country? And he answered: Nothing; but I pray you let me go. Also of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men went to Mount Seir, having as their leaders Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, son of Ishi; and they defeated the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there in their place to this day.

[Section marker: 5]

Now the sons of Reuben, firstborn of Israel — for he was indeed the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph, son of Israel, so that he is not reckoned as firstborn in the genealogy. Now Judah, who was strongest among his brothers, from his line princes arose, but the birthright was reckoned to Joseph. The sons of Reuben, firstborn of Israel: Enoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. Sons of Joel: Shemaiah his son, Gog his son, Shimei his son, Micah his son, Reaiah his son, Baal his son, Beerah his son, whom Tilgath-pileser king of Assyria carried away captive: and he was a prince in the tribe of Reuben. His brothers and all his kindred, when they were counted by their families, had as their princes Jeiel and Zechariah. Now Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel, dwelt in Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal-meon. And to the east he dwelt as far as the entrance of the wilderness and the river Euphrates, for they possessed a great number of cattle in the land of Gilead. In the days of Saul they fought against the Hagarites and killed them, and they dwelt in their tents in all the region facing east of Gilead.

The sons of Abihail: son of Uri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz. Also their brothers, sons of Abdiel son of Guni, were chiefs of their fathers' houses in their families, and they dwelt in Gilead and in Bashan and in its towns, and in all the pasturelands of Sharon to their boundaries.

...they had prepared. Concerning the vessels of the sanctuary, those who had charge of the utensils oversaw the fine flour and wine and oil and frankincense and spices. The sons of the priests prepared ointments from spices; and Mattathias the Levite, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, was set over the things that were baked in the pan. Now some of the sons of Kohath, their brethren, were over the showbread, to prepare it new every Sabbath. These are the chiefs of the singers among the families of the Levites, who dwelt in the chambers, so that day and night they might continually attend to their ministry. The heads of the Levites according to their families remained chief in Jerusalem. In Gibeon dwelt the father of Gibeon, Jehiel, and his wife's name was Maacah. His firstborn son was Abdon, and Zur and Kish and Baal and Ner and Nadab, Gedor also and Ahio and Zechariah and Mikloth. Mikloth begot Shimeah. These dwelt opposite their brethren in Jerusalem with their brethren. Ner begot Kish, and Kish begot Saul. And Saul begot Jonathan and Malchishua and Abinadab and Eshbaal. The son of Jonathan was Meribbaal, and Meribbaal begot Micah. The sons of Micah were Pithon and Melech and Tharea and Ahaz. Ahaz begot Jarah, and Jarah begot Alemeth and Azmaveth and Zimri. Zimri begot Moza, and Moza begot Binea, whose son Rephaiah begot Eleasah, from whom was born Azel. Azel had six sons with these names: Azrikam, Bocru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, Hanan. These were the sons of Azel.

Now the Philistines fought (chapter 10) against Israel, and the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell down slain on Mount Gilboa. And when the Philistines drew near, pursuing Saul and his sons, they killed Jonathan and Abinadab and Malchishua, the sons of Saul. And the battle grew fierce against Saul; and the archers found him, and wounded him with arrows. And Saul said to his armor-bearer: "Draw your sword and kill me, lest these uncircumcised come and mock me." But his armor-bearer would not do it, for he was struck with great fear. So Saul took his own sword and fell upon it. And when his armor-bearer saw that Saul was dead, he also fell upon his own sword and died. So Saul died, and his three sons, and all his house perished together. When the men of Israel who dwelt in the plains saw this, they fled; and when Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their cities and were scattered here and there; and the Philistines came and dwelt in them. And on the next day, when the Philistines came to strip the slain, they found Saul and his sons lying on Mount Gilboa. And when they had stripped him and cut off his head and stripped off his armor, they sent it throughout their land, to be carried about and shown to their idols' temples and to the people. And his armor they consecrated in the temple of their god, and they fastened his body to the wall of the temple of Dagon. When the men of Jabesh-Gilead heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul, all the valiant men rose up and took away the bodies of Saul and his sons, and brought them to Jabesh, and buried their bones under the oak that was in Jabesh, and fasted seven days. So Saul died for his iniquities, because he transgressed the commandment of the Lord which He had commanded, and did not keep it; but moreover consulted a woman who had a familiar spirit, and did not trust in the Lord: therefore He killed him, and transferred his kingdom to David the son of Jesse. (Chapter 11.)

results.translation: The sons of Judah were strengthened because they had hoped in the Lord God of their fathers. And Jeroboam pursued Abijah, but Abijah recovered the cities Jeroboam had taken: Bethel and its towns, and Jeshanah with its towns, and Ephron and its towns. Jeroboam could no longer resist in the days of Abijah, and the Lord struck him and he died. So Abijah, having strengthened his rule, took fourteen wives and begot twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters. The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and works, are written very diligently in the book of the prophet Iddo. Chapter 14. Abijah slept with his fathers and they buried him in the city of David. And Asa his son reigned in his place. In his days the land was quiet for ten years. Asa did what was good and pleasing in the sight of his God, and he overthrew the altars of foreign worship and the high places, and broke down the statues, and cut down the sacred groves. And he commanded Judah to seek the Lord God of their fathers and to observe the law and all the commandments. And he removed from all the cities of Judah the altars and shrines, and he reigned in peace. He also built fortified cities in Judah, since the land was quiet and no wars had risen in his time, the Lord granting peace. He said to Judah: Let us build these cities and surround them with walls, and let us strengthen them with towers, gates, and bars, while the land is still quiet from wars, because we have sought the Lord our God, and He has given us peace on every side. So they built, and there was no hindrance in the work. Asa had in his army men bearing shields and spears from Judah, three hundred thousand; and of Benjamin, shield-bearers and archers, two hundred and eighty thousand: all these were very strong men. And Zerah the Ethiopian came out against them with an army of a thousand thousand [a million] men and three hundred chariots, and came as far as Mareshah. Then Asa went out to meet him, and drew up his battle line in the Valley of Zephathah, which is near Mareshah, and he called upon the Lord God and said: Lord, there is no difference with You whether to help with few or with many; help us, O Lord our God, for we rely on You and in Your name we have come against this multitude. O Lord our God, let not man prevail against You. So the Lord terrified the Ethiopians before Asa and Judah, and the Ethiopians fled, and Asa and the people who were with him pursued them as far as Gerar. And the Ethiopians fell as far as utter destruction, for they were crushed before the Lord and His army fighting. So they carried off much spoil, and struck all the cities around Gerar, for great terror had fallen upon them all; and they plundered the cities and carried away much booty. They also destroyed the folds of sheep and took an infinite multitude of sheep and camels, and returned to Jerusalem. Chapter 15. Then Azariah the son of Oded, the Spirit of God having come upon him, went out to meet Asa and said to him: Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin. The Lord is with you, because you have been with Him. If you seek Him, you will find Him; but if you forsake Him, He will forsake you. Now for a long time Israel was without the true God, and without a priest to teach, and without the law. But when in their distress they turned to the Lord God of Israel and sought Him, they found Him. In that time there was no peace for him who went out or came in, but terrors were on every side among all the inhabitants of the lands. Nation fought against nation, and city against city.

...Jerusalem, imitating the fornication of the house of Ahab; moreover you have slain your brothers, the sons of your father, better men than yourself; behold, the Lord will strike you with a great plague upon yourself, your wives, and your children, and all your substance. And you shall become sick with a most grievous disease of the bowels, until your inward parts come out little by little day by day. Therefore the Lord stirred up against Joram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabians who border the Ethiopians, and they went up into the land of Judah and laid it waste. They plundered all the substance that was found in the king's house, and also his sons and his wives, so that no son was left him except Jehoahaz, his youngest. And after all these things the Lord struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels. And as days succeeded days, and the seasons of the times revolved, when the circuit of two years was completed, thus long wasted by disease, his bowels came out with the sickness, and he died in extreme misery. And the people made him no burning of spices according to custom, as they had done for his ancestors. He was thirty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He walked not uprightly, and they buried him in the city of David, but not in the sepulchre of the kings. Chapter 22.
The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, for the raiders of Arabs who had burst into the camp had slain all the elder ones before him. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned; he was forty-two years old when he began to reign, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri. He also walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother incited him to act wickedly. So he did evil in the sight of the Lord, as the house of Ahab did. For they were his counselors after the death of his father, to his ruin, and he walked in their counsels. He went also with Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead; and the Syrians wounded Joram. He returned to be healed at Jezreel, for he had received many wounds in the aforesaid battle. Therefore Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to visit Joram son of Ahab, who was sick in Jezreel. Now it was the will of God against Ahaziah, that he should come to Joram. And when he had come and went out with him against Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the Lord had anointed to destroy the house of Ahab, then, as Jehu was executing judgment upon the house of Ahab, he found the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah who served him, and slew them. And seeking Ahaziah himself, he found him hiding in Samaria, and having been brought to him he killed him; and they buried him, because he was the son of Jehoshaphat, who had sought the Lord with all his heart. And there was no further hope that any of the seed should reign over Ahaziah. For when his mother Athaliah saw that her son was dead, she rose up and destroyed all the royal seed of the house of Joram. But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah, and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being slain, and hid him with his nurse in the bedchamber; now Jehoshabeath who had hidden him was the daughter of King Joram, wife of Jehoiada the priest, sister of Ahaziah; and therefore Athaliah did not kill him. So he remained hidden with them in the house of God six years, during which Athaliah reigned over the land. Chapter 23.

It records that certain priestly families could not prove their genealogy and were therefore excluded from the priesthood, being told by the governor (Athersatha) not to eat of the most holy things until a priest with Urim and Thummim should arise. They kept the Feast of Tabernacles as it is written, with daily burnt offerings according to the ordinance, each on its proper day, and thereafter the continual burnt offering, on new moons and at all the sacred feasts of the Lord, and whenever a freewill offering was made to the Lord. The mother who bore them says to them: Go, my children, for I am a widow and forsaken. I brought you up with gladness: and I have lost you with mourning and sadness. Because you have sinned before the Lord your God, and have done evil before me. Now what shall I do to you? I am a widow and forsaken. Go, children, and seek mercy from the Lord. But I, father, rightly call upon you against the mother of the children, who would not keep my testament: that you may give them confusion and their mother to plunder: let there be no generation of them. Let them be scattered among the nations, let their name be blotted out from the earth - because they have despised my covenant. Woe to you, Assyria, who hide the wicked who seek you. God, remember what I did to Sodom and Gomorrah, whose land lies in pitchy clods and heaps of ashes. Thus I will make those who have not heard me: says the Lord almighty. And I will take their glory to myself, and give them eternal tabernacles which I had prepared for them; the tree of life will be there for them in the odor of ointment: and they will not labor nor grow weary. Seminis quantum fructum impietatis generauit: quando seminate fuerit spice quarum non est numerus, quia magna area incipiet facere. Et respondi et dixi. Quousque et quando hec? Quare modici et mali anni nostri? Et respondit ad me, et dixit michi. Non festines tu super altissimum. Tu enim festinas inaniter esse super ipsum. Nam excessus tuus multus. Nonne de hijs interrogauerunt anime iustorum in promptuarijs suis dicentes: usquequo spero sic, et quando veniet fructus aree mercedis nostre? Et respondit ad ea Ieremiel archangelus et dixit. Quando impletus fuerit numerus seminum nobis: quoniam in statera ponderauit seculum et mensura mensurauit tempora, et numero numerauit tempora: et non commouit nec excitauit usque dum impleatur predicta mensura. Et respondi et dixi. Dominator domine: sed et nos omnes pleni sumus impietate. Et ne forte propter nos non impleantur iustorum aree: propter peccata inhabitantium super terram. Et respondit ad me, et dixit. Vade et interroga pregnantem: si quando impleuerit nouem menses suos, adhuc poterit matrix eius retinere partum in semetipsa. Et dixi. Non potest domine. Et dixit ad me. In inferno promptuaria animarum, matrici assimulata sunt. Quemadmodum enim illa festinat que parit effugere necessitatem partus: sic et hec festinat reddere ea que commendata sunt. Ab initio tibi demonstrabit de hijs que concupiscis videre. Et respondi et dixi. Si inueni gratiam ante oculos tuos, et si possibile est et si idoneus sum: demonstra michi si plus quam preteritum sit habere venire: aut plura preterierunt supra quam futurum est. Quid preterierit scio: quid autem futurus sit ignoro. Et dixit ad me. Sta super dexteram partem: et demonstrabo tibi interpretationem similitudinis. Et steti et vidi: et ecce fornax ardens transiit coram me. Et factum est cum transiret flamma: vidi et ecce supercreuit fumus. Post hec transiit coram me nubes plena aque: et immisit pluuiam impetu multam. Et cum transisset impetus pluuie: superauerunt in ea gutte. Et dixit ad me. Cogita tibi. Sicut crescit pluuia amplius quam gutte, et ignis quam fumus: sic superabundauit que transiuit mensura. Superauerunt autem gutte et fumus. Et oraui et dixi. Putas viuo usque in diebus illis? Vel quis erit in diebus illis? Respondit ad me et dixit. De signis de quibus me interrogas ex parte possum tibi dicere: de vita autem tua non sum missus dicere tibi: sed nescio.

De signis autem: ecce dies venient in quibus apprehendent qui inhabitant terram intensu metu: et abscondetur veritatis via, et sterilis erit a fide regio: et multiplicabitur iniusticia super hanc quam ipse tu vides et super quam audisti olim: et erit imposito vestigio quam nunc vides regnare regione: et videbunt eam desertam. Si autem tibi dederit altissimus vivere videbis post terciam turbam: et relucescet subito sol noctu, et luna ter in die: et de ligno sanguis stillabit, et lapis dabit vocem suam: et populi commouebuntur, et regnabit quem non sperant qui inhabitant super terram: et volatilia commigrationem facient: et mare Sodomiticum pisces reiiciet: et dabit vocem noctu quam non nouerant multi. Omnes autem audient vocem eius. Et chaos fiet pro loca multa, et ignis frequenter remittetur: et bestie agrestes transmigrabunt: et mulieres menstruate pariunt monstra: et in dulcibus aquis salse invenientur: et amici omnes in semetipsos oppugnabunt.

How much fruit of iniquity the seed has produced, when the ears of grain shall have been sown, of which there is no number, because the threshing-floor will begin to grow great. And I answered and said: How long, and when shall these things be? Why are our years few and evil? And he answered me, and said to me: Do not hasten faster than the Most High. For you hasten in vain to be above him. For your haste is very great. Have not the souls of the righteous in their chambers asked concerning these things, saying: How long shall I hope thus, and when shall the fruit of the threshing-floor of our reward come? And the archangel Jeremiel answered them and said: When the number of the seed destined for you shall be fulfilled: for he has weighed the age in the balance, and measured the times by measure, and numbered the seasons by number: and he will not move nor stir until the aforesaid measure is fulfilled. And I answered and said: O Sovereign Lord, but we all are full of iniquity. And perhaps because of us the threshing-floors of the righteous are not filled, on account of the sins of those who dwell on the earth. And he answered me and said: Go and ask a pregnant woman whether, when she has completed her nine months, the womb can still retain the child within itself. And I said: It cannot, Lord. And he said to me: In the underworld the chambers of souls are like the womb. For just as a woman in labor hastens to escape the necessity of childbirth, so also these hasten to give back what has been entrusted to them. From the beginning he will show you concerning the things you desire to see. And I answered and said: If I have found grace in your sight, and if it is possible, and if I am worthy, show me whether more time remains than has passed, or whether more has passed than is yet to come. What has passed I know, but what is to come I do not know. And he said to me: Stand on the right side, and I will show you the interpretation of a likeness. And I stood and saw, and behold, a burning furnace passed before me. And it happened that as the flame passed, I saw, and behold, smoke rose up. After this a cloud full of water passed before me, and sent down much rain with force. And when the force of the rain had passed, drops still remained in it. And he said to me: Consider this — as the rain is greater than the drops, and the fire than the smoke, so the measure that passed exceeded; but the drops and the smoke remained. And I prayed and said: Do you suppose I shall live until those days? Or who shall be in those days? He answered me and said: Concerning the signs about which you ask me, I can tell you in part; but concerning your life I have not been sent to tell you — I do not know.

But concerning the signs: behold, days shall come in which those who dwell on the earth shall be seized with great fear, and the way of truth shall be hidden, and the land shall be barren of faith; and iniquity shall be multiplied beyond what you now see and beyond what you have heard of old; and the land which you now see ruling shall be laid waste, its former glory trodden underfoot, and they shall see it deserted. But if the Most High grants you to live, you shall see it thrown into confusion after the third period: and the sun shall suddenly shine forth by night, and the moon three times in the day: and blood shall drip from wood, and the stone shall utter its voice: the peoples shall be troubled, and he whom the inhabitants of the earth do not expect shall reign: the birds shall migrate away; the Sea of Sodom shall cast up fish; and one shall utter a voice by night which many do not know, and all shall hear its voice. And chaos shall come upon many places; fire shall often break forth; wild beasts shall wander from their haunts; women shall bring forth monsters; salt water shall be found in sweet springs; and all friends shall make war upon one another.

Great art thou, O Lord, forever, and thy kingdom is over all ages: for thou dost scourge and save, thou leadest down to hell and bringest back, and there is none that can escape thy hand. Give praise to the Lord, ye children of Israel, and praise him in the sight of the nations: for he hath therefore scattered you among the nations who know him not, that you may declare his wonderful works, and make them know that there is no other almighty God besides him. He hath chastised us for our iniquities, and he will save us for his own mercy. Behold then what he hath done with us, and with fear and trembling give ye glory to him: and extol the king of the world in your works. As for me, I will praise him in the land of my captivity: because he hath shown his majesty toward a sinful nation. Be converted therefore, ye sinners, and do justice before God, believing that he will show his mercy to you. And I and my soul will rejoice in him. Bless the Lord, all ye his chosen ones: keep days of joy, and give praise to him. O Jerusalem, city of God, the Lord hath chastised thee for the works of thy hands. Give praise to the Lord for thy good things, and bless the God of ages, that he may rebuild his tabernacle in thee, and may call back to thee all that are captives, and thou mayest rejoice for all ages of ages. Thou shalt shine with a glorious light, and all the ends of the earth shall worship thee. Nations from afar shall come to thee, and bringing gifts they shall adore the Lord in thee, and shall regard thy land as holy. For they shall call upon the great name in thee. Cursed shall be all they that shall despise thee: and condemned shall be all they that shall blaspheme thee: and blessed shall be they that shall build thee up. But thou shalt rejoice in thy children, because they shall all be blessed and shall be gathered together to the Lord. Blessed are all they that love thee, and that rejoice in thy peace. My soul, bless thou the Lord, because he hath delivered Jerusalem his city. Happy shall I be if there shall remain of my seed to see the glory of Jerusalem. The gates of Jerusalem shall be built of sapphire and of emerald, and all the walls thereof round about of precious stone. All its streets shall be paved with white and clean stones: and Alleluia shall be sung in its streets. Blessed be the Lord who hath exalted it, that his kingdom may be over it forever and ever. Amen. And the words of Tobias were ended. And after he received his sight, Tobias lived forty-two years, and saw the sons of his grandchildren. And when he had completed a hundred and two years, he was buried honorably in Nineveh. For he was fifty-six years old when he lost the light of his eyes, and he received it again when he was sixty. The rest of his life was in joy, and he went forward in the fear of God, with good progress, and he departed in peace. Now in the hour of his death he called to him Tobias his son, and his seven sons his grandchildren, and said to them: Destruction is near for Nineveh. For the word of the Lord shall not fail: and our brethren who are scattered from the land of Israel shall return to it. And all its land, now deserted, shall be filled again; and the house of God which was burnt in it shall be rebuilt again: and thither shall return all that fear God. And the nations shall leave their idols, and shall come into Jerusalem, and shall dwell in it; and all the kings of the earth shall rejoice in it, worshiping the King of Israel. Hear therefore, my sons, your father. Serve the Lord in truth, and seek to do what is pleasing to him. And command your children to do justice and alms, that they may be mindful of God and bless him at all times in truth and with all their strength.

...I would not have raised my spear against him. But now tell me for what reason you departed from them, and it pleased you to come to us. And Judith said to him: Take the words of your handmaid, for if you follow the words of your handmaid, the Lord will accomplish a perfect thing with you. For Nebuchadnezzar the king of the earth lives, and his power lives, which is in you for the correction of all wandering souls, for not only do men serve him because of you, but even the beasts of the field obey him. For the industry of your mind is reported to all nations, and it has been made known in every age that you alone are good and powerful in his whole kingdom, and that your discipline is proclaimed in all provinces. Nor is it hidden what Achior spoke, nor is it unknown what you commanded to happen to him. For it is certain that our God has been so offended by sins that He has commanded through His prophets to the people that He would hand him over for their sins. And because the sons of Israel know that they have offended their God, terror of you is upon them. Moreover, famine has also invaded them, and from lack of water they are now counted among the dead. Finally, they have determined to kill their own cattle and drink their blood, and to touch the sacred things of their Lord which God commanded not to be touched—the grain, wine, and oil. These things they have determined to spend, and wish to consume that which they ought not touch with their hands. Therefore since they do this, it is certain that they will be given over to destruction. Not I, your handmaid, knowing this, fled from them, and the Lord sent me to announce these very things to you. For I, your handmaid, worship God even now with you, and your handmaid will go out and pray to God, and He will tell me when He will repay their sin; and coming I will announce it to you, so that I may lead you through the midst of Jerusalem. And you will have all Israel itself like sheep who have no shepherd, and not even one dog will bark against you, for these things have been told to me through the providence of God. And because God is angry with them, I have been sent to announce this to you. Now all these words pleased Holofernes and before his servants, and they marveled at her wisdom, and said to one another: There is no such woman upon earth in appearance, in beauty, and in sense of words. And Holofernes said to her: God has done well who sent you before the people, that you might give them into our hands. And because your promise is good, if your God does this for me, He shall be my God also, and you shall be great in the house of Nebuchadnezzar, and your name shall be named in all the earth.

And all who adored the Lord said to her: The Lord has blessed you in His power, for through you He has brought our enemies to nothing. Then Ozias, the prince of the people of Israel, said to her: Blessed are you, daughter, by the Lord God Most High, above all women upon the earth. Blessed be the Lord who created heaven and earth, who directed you to the wounds of the head of the prince of our enemies; for today He has so magnified your name that your praise shall not depart from the mouth of men who shall remember the power of the Lord forever, for whom you did not spare your own life amid the anguish and tribulation of your people, but relieved their ruin in the sight of our God. And all the people said: So be it, so be it. Then Achior, being called, came. And she said to him: The God of Israel, to whom you gave testimony that He avenges Himself upon His enemies, has this very night, by my hand, cut off the head of all the unbelievers. And that you may know it is true: behold the head of Holofernes, who in the contempt of his pride despised the God of Israel and threatened you with death, saying: When the people of Israel are captured, I will command your sides to be pierced with the sword. But when Achior saw the head of Holofernes, overcome with fear he fell upon his face on the ground and his spirit fainted. But afterward, when his spirit was recovered and he was revived, he fell down at her feet and worshipped her, and said: Blessed are you by your God in every tabernacle of Jacob; for in every nation that hears your name, the God of Israel shall be magnified because of you. Then Judith said to all the people: Hear me, brethren. Hang up this head upon our walls; and when the sun rises, let every man take up his weapons and go out with a rush—not as though going down, but making an assault. Then the scouts will be forced to flee to their prince to rouse him to battle. And when their leaders run to the tent of Holofernes and find him a headless trunk wallowing in his own blood, fear shall fall upon them. And when they know that these men flee, pursue them with the sword; for the Lord will crush them under your feet. Then Achior, seeing the power which the God of Israel had wrought, abandoning the rite of his heathen people, believed in God and circumcised the flesh of his foreskin, and was joined to the people of Israel, and all his descendants, even to this day. And as soon as day broke, they hung the head of Holofernes upon the walls; and every man took up his arms, and they went out with a great noise and shouting. Seeing this, the scouts ran to the tent. And those who were in the tent came and, before entering the chamber, made noise outside so as to rouse him not by shaking him but by the sound, so that Holofernes might wake. For no one dared to open the chamber of the mighty Assyrian by knocking or entering. Judith

... of our people. Assur (Nebuchadnezzar's general) came from the mountains from the north with the multitude of his strength, whose multitude blocked up the torrents and the horses covered the valleys. He said he would burn my borders and slay my young men with the sword, give my infants for prey, and my virgins into captivity. But the Lord Almighty harmed him and delivered him into the hands of a woman, and confounded him. For their mighty one did not fall by young men, nor did the sons of Titans strike him, nor did tall giants set upon him, but Judith daughter of Merari dissolved him by the beauty of her face. For she put off the garments of widowhood and put on garments of gladness for the exaltation of the sons of Israel. She anointed her face with ointment, bound her locks with a headband to deceive him. Her sandals ravished his eyes, her beauty made his soul captive; she cut off his head with a sword. The Persians shuddered at her constancy, and the Medes at her boldness. Then the camps of the Assyrians howled when my humble ones appeared, wasting away with thirst. The sons of maidens pierced them, and killed them as though fleeing boys; they perished in the battle before the face of the Lord my God. Let us sing a hymn to the Lord, let us sing a new hymn to our God. Adonai, Lord, you are great and glorious in power, whom none can overcome. Let all your creation serve you, for you spoke and they were made; you sent forth your spirit and they were created; and there is none who can resist your voice. The mountains shall be moved from their foundations with the waters; the rocks shall melt like wax before your face. But those who fear you shall be great before you in all things. Woe to the nation that rises up against my people. For the Lord Almighty will avenge himself upon them, and on the day of judgment he will visit them. He will give fire and worms into their flesh, that they may burn and feel it forever.

And it came to pass after this that all the people, after the victory, came to Jerusalem to worship the Lord; and as soon as they were purified, they all offered holocausts, and their vows, and their freewill offerings. Moreover Judith placed among the things devoted to oblivion all the weapons of Holofernes which he had given her, and the canopy which she herself had taken. And there was joy among them according to the appearance of the holy days, and for three months the joy of this victory was celebrated with Judith. But after those days each returned to his own home; and Judith became great in Bethulia, and was more renowned than all the land of Israel. She also had virtue joined to chastity, so that she knew no man all the days of her life, from the time her husband Manasses died. She was present on the feast days with great glory. She remained in her husband's house one hundred and five years, and set her handmaid free; and she died and was buried with her husband in Bethulia, and all the people mourned her seven days. In all the time of her life there was none who troubled Israel, nor for many years after her death. But the day of the victory of this festival is received by the Hebrews in the number of holy days, and is observed by the Jews from that time even to the present day.

Then Eliphaz the Temanite answered and said: Can a man be compared to God, even one who is perfect in knowledge? What does it profit God if you be just, or what do you add to him if your life be spotless? Will he reprove you for fear, and come with you into judgment, and not because of your great wickedness and infinite iniquities? For you have taken pledges of your brothers without cause, and stripped the naked of their clothing. You gave no water to the weary, and withheld bread from the hungry. By the strength of your arm you possessed the land, and being most mighty you held it. You sent widows away empty, and broke the arms of the fatherless. Therefore you are surrounded by snares, and sudden fear troubles you. And you thought you should not see darkness, and should not be overwhelmed by the rush of overflowing waters. Do you think God is higher than heaven, and exalted above the height of the stars? And you say: What does God know? He judges as it were through a mist. Clouds are his hiding place, and he does not consider our things, and he walks about the poles of heaven. Will you keep to the path which wicked men have trodden, who were taken away before their time, and whose foundation a flood overthrew? Who said to God: Depart from us; and thought the Almighty could do nothing, when yet he had filled their houses with good things. May their counsel be far from me. The just shall see it and rejoice, and the innocent shall laugh them to scorn. Shall not their haughtiness be cut down, and shall not fire devour their remnant? Agree therefore with him and have peace, and thereby you shall have excellent fruits. Receive the law from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart. If you return to the Almighty, you shall be built up, and you shall put iniquity far from your tent. He shall give you flint for earth, and for flint, streams of gold. And the Almighty shall be against your enemies, and he shall heap up silver for you. Then you shall abound in delights in the Almighty, and shall lift up your face to God. You shall pray to him, and he will hear you, and you shall pay your vows. You shall decree a thing, and it shall come to you, and light shall shine on your ways. For he has said, 'A man will not please God, even though he should run with Him.' Therefore, wise men, hear me. Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to commit iniquity. Who has appointed another over the earth, or placed anyone over the whole world which He made? If He should set His heart upon a man, He would draw to Himself his spirit and breath. All flesh would perish together, and man would return to dust. Therefore, if you have understanding, hear what is said, and listen to the voice of my words. Can he who hates judgment be healed? And how do you so condemn Him who is just? He who says to a king, 'You are wicked,' who calls rulers ungodly; who does not respect the persons of princes, nor regards the powerful more than the poor when they contend, for they are all the work of His hands. Suddenly they shall die, and the people shall be troubled at midnight and shall pass away; and He shall take away the mighty without a hand. For His eyes are upon the ways of men, and He considers all their steps. There is no darkness, nor shadow of death, where the workers of iniquity may hide themselves. For it is not in man's power to come into judgment with God. He shall break in pieces many that are without number, and set others in their place. For He knows their works; therefore He shall bring the night, and they shall be crushed. He strikes the wicked openly, in a place where they are seen — those who purposely departed from Him and would not understand any of His ways, so that they caused the cry of the poor to come to Him, and He heard the voice of the afflicted. For when He gives peace, who can condemn? And when He hides His face, who can behold Him, whether it be over nations or over all men alike? He makes a hypocrite to reign because of the sins of the people. Now because I have spoken to God, I will not restrain myself further. If I have erred, teach me. If I have spoken iniquity, I will add no more. Does God require it of you because it displeased you? For you began to speak, not I. But if you know better, then speak. Let men of understanding speak to me, and let a wise man listen to me. But Job has spoken foolishly, and his words do not sound of wisdom. My Father, let Job be tried to the end, and do not cease from a man of iniquity who adds blasphemy to his sins. Let him therefore be restrained among us, and let him call God to judgment with all his own.

Then Elihu spoke again thus: 'Does it seem right to you that you should say, I am more righteous than God? For you have said, What is right does not please you. There is no power on earth that can be compared to him, who was made to fear nothing. He beholds all high things; he is king over all the sons of pride. Chapter 41.

Then Job answered the Lord and said: I know that thou canst do all things, and no thought is hid from thee. Who is this that hides counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have spoken unwisely, and things that exceeded my knowledge beyond measure. Hear, and I will speak; I will ask thee, and answer thou me. I had heard of thee by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees thee. Therefore I reprehend myself, and do penance in dust and ashes. And after the Lord had spoken these words to Job, he said to Eliphaz the Themanite: My wrath is kindled against thee and against thy two friends, because you have not spoken before me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath. Take therefore unto you seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. And Job my servant shall pray for you: his face I will accept, that folly be not imputed to you, for you have not spoken right things concerning me as my servant Job hath. So Eliphaz the Themanite, and Baldad the Suhite, and Sophar the Naamathite went and did as the Lord had spoken to them, and the Lord accepted the face of Job. The Lord also was turned to the penance of Job when he prayed for his friends. And the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before. And there came to him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all that knew him before, and they ate bread with him in his house, and they condoled with him and comforted him upon all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him;

and every one gave him a sheep, and one earring of gold. And the Lord blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning: and he had fourteen thousand sheep, and six thousand camels, and a thousand yoke of oxen, and a thousand she-asses. And he had seven sons and three daughters. And he called the name of the first Day, and the name of the second Cassia, and the name of the third Cornstibium. And no women were found so beautiful as the daughters of Job in all the earth: and their father gave them inheritance among their brethren. And Job lived after this a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and his sons' sons unto the fourth generation, and died being old and full of days.

Here ends the Book of Job. Here begins the prologue of blessed Jerome the priest on the Psalter.
I had long ago at Rome corrected the Psalter, and according to the Septuagint interpreters, though hastily, yet for the most part had amended it. But since you now see, O Paula and Eustochium, that it has again been corrupted by the fault of scribes, and that the old error prevails more than the new correction avails, you beg me that as it were in some fallow ground I might now cultivate the field already tilled, and by cross furrows root out the thorns springing up again, judging it fair that what often sprouts should be more often mown down. Unless you turn back, he has whetted his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready. And in it he has prepared instruments of death; he has made his arrows fiery. Behold, he has conceived injustice; he has conceived sorrow and brought forth iniquity. He has opened a pit and dug it: and he has fallen into the hole which he made. His sorrow shall be turned upon his own head, and his wickedness shall descend upon his own crown. To the end, a psalm of David concerning the wine-presses. VIII.
O Lord our God, how admirable is your name in all the earth! For your magnificence is exalted above the heavens. Out of the mouths of infants and of those who suckle you have perfected praise, because of your enemies, that you might destroy the enemy and the avenger. For I will see your heavens, the works of your fingers, the moon and the stars which you have founded. What is man that you are mindful of him, or the son of man that you visit him? You have made him a little lower than the angels: you have crowned him with glory and honor and set him over the works of your hands. You have subjected all things under his feet: all sheep and oxen, and also the beasts of the field; the birds of the air and the fish of the sea, which pass through the paths of the sea. O Lord our God, how admirable is your name in all the earth!

He shall be equal to the Lord: he shall be like unto God among the sons of God. God, who is glorified in the council of the saints: great and terrible above all that are round about him. O Lord God of hosts, who is like unto thee? Thou art mighty, O Lord, and thy truth is round about thee. Thou rulest the power of the sea: thou stillest the swelling of the waves thereof. Thou hast humbled the proud one as one that is slain: with the arm of thy strength thou hast scattered thine enemies. The heavens are thine, and the earth is thine: thou hast founded the world and the fullness thereof; thou hast created the north and the sea. Tabor and Hermon shall rejoice in thy name: thine arm with power. Let thy hand be strengthened and thy right hand exalted: justice and judgment are the preparation of thy seat. Mercy and truth shall go before thy face: blessed is the people that knoweth jubilation. O Lord, they shall walk in the light of thy countenance: and in thy name they shall rejoice all the day, and in thy justice they shall be exalted. For thou art the glory of their strength: and in thy good pleasure our horn shall be exalted. For our shield is of the Lord, and the holy one of Israel our king. Then thou spakest in a vision to thy saints, and saidst: I have laid help upon one that is mighty: and have exalted one chosen out of my people. I have found David my servant: with my holy oil I have anointed him. For my hand shall help him: and my arm shall strengthen him. The enemy shall have no advantage over him: nor the son of iniquity have power to hurt him. And I will beat down his enemies before his face: and them that hate him I will put to flight. And my truth and my mercy shall be with him: and in my name shall his horn be exalted. I will set his hand in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers. He shall call upon me: Thou art my father, my God, and the support of my salvation. And I will make him my firstborn: high above the kings of the earth.

I will keep my mercy for him forever: and my covenant faithful with him. And I will make his seed to endure forever, and his throne as the days of heaven. But if his children forsake my law: and walk not in my judgments. If they profane my justices: and keep not my commandments. I will visit their iniquities with a rod: and their sins with stripes. But my mercy I will not take away from him: nor suffer my truth to fail. Neither will I profane my covenant: and the words that proceed from my mouth I will not make void. Once have I sworn by my holiness: I will not lie unto David. His seed shall endure forever. And his throne as the sun before me: and as the moon perfect forever, and a faithful witness in heaven. But thou hast rejected and despised: thou hast delayed thine anointed. Thou hast overthrown the covenant of thy servant: thou hast profaned his sanctuary on the earth. Thou hast broken down all his hedges: thou hast made his strength fear. All that pass by the way have spoiled him: he is become a reproach to his neighbors. Thou hast set up the right hand of them that oppress him: thou hast made all his enemies to rejoice. Thou hast turned away the help of his sword: and hast not assisted him in battle. Thou hast made his purification to cease: and cast his throne down to the ground. Thou hast shortened the days of his time: thou hast covered him with confusion. How long, O Lord, turnest thou away unto the end? Shall thy wrath burn like fire? Remember what my substance is: for hast thou made all the children of men in vain? Who is the man that shall live and not see death: shall he deliver his soul from the hand of hell? Lord, where are thy ancient mercies, according to what thou didst swear to David in thy truth? Remember, O Lord, the reproach of thy servants which I have kept in my bosom, of many nations.

results.translation:
The Lord is just and our God is merciful. The Lord preserves the little ones; I was humbled and He delivered me. Return, O my soul, to your rest, for the Lord has been bountiful to you. For He has delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, my feet from falling. I will please the Lord in the land of the living. Alleluia.

I believed, therefore have I spoken; but I was greatly humbled. I said in my excess: every man is a liar. What shall I render to the Lord for all He has rendered to me? I will take the chalice of salvation and call upon the name of the Lord. I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all His people; precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints. O Lord, for I am your servant; I am your servant and the son of your handmaid. You have broken my bonds; I will sacrifice to You the sacrifice of praise and will call upon the name of the Lord. I will pay my vows to the Lord in the sight of all His people, in the courts of the house of the Lord, in the midst of you, O Jerusalem. Alleluia.

Praise the Lord, all nations; praise Him, all people. For His mercy is confirmed upon us, and the truth of the Lord remains forever. Alleluia.

Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever. Let Israel now say that He is good, for His mercy endures forever. Let the house of Aaron now say that His mercy endures forever. Let those who fear the Lord now say that His mercy endures forever. In my trouble I called upon the Lord, and He heard me and set me in a wide place. The Lord is my helper; I will not fear what man can do to me. The Lord is my helper, and I shall look down upon my enemies. It is good to trust in the Lord rather than to trust in man. It is good to hope in the Lord rather than to hope in princes. All nations surrounded me, but in the name of the Lord I took vengeance on them. They surrounded me and compassed me about; in the name of the Lord I took vengeance on them. They surrounded me like bees and were burned like fire among thorns; in the name of the Lord I took vengeance on them. I was pushed hard so as to fall, but the Lord upheld me. My strength and my praise is the Lord, and He has become my salvation. The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous. The right hand of the Lord has done mighty deeds; the right hand of the Lord has exalted me; the right hand of the Lord has done mighty deeds. I shall not die but live, and I shall declare the works of the Lord. The Lord has chastened me severely, but has not delivered me to death. Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter into them and give praise to the Lord. This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter into it. I will give thanks to You, for You have heard me and have become my salvation. The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. This is the Lord's doing, and it is marvelous in our eyes. This is the day which the Lord has made; let us rejoice and be glad in it. O Lord, save me; O Lord, send prosperity. Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. We have blessed you from the house of the Lord. God is the Lord and has shone upon us. Appoint a solemn day with thick boughs, up to the horns of the altar. You are my God and I will give thanks to You; You are my God and I will exalt You. I will give thanks to You, for You have heard me and have become my salvation. Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever. Alleluia. Aleph. 119.

Blessed are the undefiled in the way, who walk in the law of the Lord. Blessed are they who search out His testimonies, who seek Him with their whole heart. For those who work iniquity have not walked in His ways. You have commanded that Your commandments be kept diligently. Oh that my ways may be directed to keep...

your law. Your testimonies were made songs to me in the place of my pilgrimage. I remembered your name, O Lord, in the night, and kept your law. This was done to me: because I sought your justifications. Heth.
O Lord, my portion, I have said that I would keep your law. I entreated your face with my whole heart: have mercy on me according to your word. I have thought on my ways, and turned my feet unto your testimonies. I am ready and am not troubled, that I may keep your commandments. The cords of sinners have entangled me: but I have not forgotten your law. At midnight I rose to confess to you, because of the judgments of your justification. I am a partaker with all them that fear you, and that keep your commandments. The earth, O Lord, is full of your mercy: teach me your justifications. Teth.
You have dealt well with your servant, O Lord, according to your word. Teach me goodness and discipline and knowledge: for I have believed your commandments. Before I was humbled I offended: therefore have I kept your word. You are good, and in your goodness teach me your justifications. The iniquity of the proud has been multiplied upon me: but I will seek your commandments with my whole heart. Their heart is curdled like milk: but I have meditated on your law. It is good for me that you have humbled me, that I may learn your justifications. The law of your mouth is good to me above thousands of gold and silver. Ioth.
Your hands have made me and formed me: give me understanding, that I may learn your commandments. They that fear you shall see me and be glad: because I have hoped in your words. I know, O Lord, that your judgments are equity, and in your truth you have humbled me. Let your mercy be for my comfort, according to your word to your servant.

[Right column]
Let your mercies come to me, and I shall live: for your law is my meditation. Let the proud be confounded, because they have done unjustly against me: but I will be occupied in your commandments. Let those that fear you turn to me, and they that know your testimonies. Let my heart be undefiled in your justifications, that I be not confounded. Caph.
My soul has fainted for your salvation: and I have hoped exceedingly in your word. My eyes have failed for your word, saying: When will you comfort me? For I have become like a bottle in the frost: I have not forgotten your justifications. How many are the days of your servant: when will you execute judgment on them that persecute me? The wicked have told me fables: but not as your law. All your commandments are truth: they have persecuted me unjustly, help me. They had almost consumed me upon earth: but I have not forsaken your commandments. Quicken me according to your mercy: and I shall keep the testimonies of your mouth. Lameth.
For ever, O Lord, your word stands firm in heaven. Your truth endures to all generations: you have founded the earth, and it continues. By your ordinance the day goes on: for all things serve you. Unless your law had been my meditation, I would then have perished in my abasement. I will never forget your justifications: for by them you have given me life. I am yours, save me: for I have sought your justifications. The wicked have waited for me to destroy me: but I have understood your testimonies. I have seen an end of all perfection: your commandment is exceedingly broad. Mem.
O how have I loved your law, O Lord! It is my meditation all the day. Through your commandment, you have made me wiser than my enemies: for it is ever with me. I have understood above all that taught me: for your testimonies are my meditation.

It will lay them waste. Riches will not profit in the day of vengeance, but righteousness delivers from death. The righteousness of the upright shall direct his way, but the wicked shall fall by his own wickedness. The righteousness of the upright shall deliver them, but the treacherous shall be caught by their own snares. When a wicked man dies, hope perishes, and the expectation of the anxious comes to nothing. The just man is delivered from distress, and the wicked man is handed over in his place. The hypocrite deceives his friend with his mouth, but the righteous shall be delivered by knowledge. In the good of the righteous the city rejoices, and in the destruction of the wicked there is jubilation. By the blessing of the upright the city is exalted, but by the mouth of the wicked it is overthrown. He who despises his neighbor lacks sense, but a prudent man keeps silent. He who walks about as a talebearer reveals secrets, but he who is faithful conceals a matter. Where there is no guide the people fall, but safety comes with many counselors. He who is surety for a stranger will suffer harm, but he who hates suretyship is secure. A gracious woman gets honor, and strong men get riches. A merciful man does good to his own soul, but he who is cruel troubles his own flesh and cuts off his kin. The wicked does unstable work, but he who sows righteousness has a sure reward. Mercy prepares life, but the pursuit of evil leads to death. A false heart is abominable to the Lord, but his will is with those who walk sincerely. Hand joined to hand shall not go unpunished for evil; but the seed of the righteous shall be saved. A jewel of gold in a swine's snout is a beautiful and foolish woman. The desire of the righteous is wholly good, but the expectation of the wicked is wrath. Some distribute their own goods and become richer, others seize what is not theirs and are always in need. A liberal soul shall be made fat, and he who satisfies others shall himself be satisfied. He who withholds grain, the people will curse him: but blessing shall be upon the head of him who sells it. He rises well early who seeks good things, but he who searches out evil, evil shall come upon him. He who trusts in his riches shall fall, but the just shall flourish like a green leaf. He who troubles his own house shall inherit the wind, and the fool shall serve the wise. The fruit of the just is a tree of life, and he who wins souls is wise. If the just man is recompensed on earth, how much more the wicked and the sinner. Chapter 12.

He who loves discipline loves knowledge, but he who hates reproof is foolish. He who is good draws favor from the Lord, but he who trusts in his own devices acts wickedly. Man shall not be established by wickedness, and the root of the righteous shall not be moved. A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband, but she who acts shamefully is like rottenness in his bones. The thoughts of the righteous are just, but the counsels of the wicked are deceitful. The words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them. Overturn the wicked and they shall not be, but the house of the righteous shall endure. A man is known by his own doctrine, but he who is vain and senseless shall be exposed to contempt. Better is the poor man who is content with himself than the glorious man who lacks bread. The righteous man knows the souls of his beasts, but the bowels of the wicked are cruel. He who tills his own land shall be satisfied with bread, but he who pursues idleness is most foolish. He who is fond of pleasures lives in excess; in his own admonitions he leaves reproach. The desire of the wicked is a monument of the worst things, but the root of the righteous shall prosper. Because of the sins of the lips, ruin draws near to the evil man, but the righteous shall escape from distress. From the fruit of his mouth each man shall be filled with good things, and according to the works of his hands it shall be repaid to him. The way of a fool is right in his own eyes

Better is a little with the fear of the Lord than great treasures and unrest. Better is a dinner of herbs with love than a fatted calf with hatred. A wise son makes his father glad; but a foolish man despises his mother. Folly is joy to a fool; but a prudent man directs his steps. Evil thoughts are an abomination to the Lord, but pure words shall be strengthened by him. He who follows after greed troubles his own house; but he who hates gifts shall live. The fear of the Lord is the discipline of wisdom, and humility goes before glory. Chapter 16. It belongs to man to prepare the soul, and to the Lord to govern the tongue. All the ways of man are open to his eyes; the Lord is the weigher of spirits. Commit your works to the Lord, and your thoughts shall be directed. The Lord has made all things for himself, even the wicked for the evil day. Every arrogant one is an abomination to the Lord; even if hand joins hand, he shall not be innocent. The beginning of a good way is to do justice; it is more acceptable to God than to offer sacrifices. By mercy and truth iniquity is redeemed; and by the fear of the Lord men turn away from evil. When a man's ways please the Lord, he will turn even his enemies to peace. Better is a little with justice than great fruits with iniquity. results.translation:
Proverbs.

He who is wise will understand wisdom. He who afflicts his father and flees his mother shall be shameful and unfortunate. Do not cease to hear, son, instruction; nor ignore the words of knowledge. An unjust witness will cause judgment to fall; and the mouth of the wicked devours iniquity. Judgments are prepared for scoffers, and hammers striking upon the bodies of fools. Chapter 20.

Wine is a luxurious thing, and drunkenness is tumultuous. Whoever delights in these will not be wise. Like the roaring of a lion, so is the terror of a king; he who provokes him sins against his own soul. It is an honor for a man to separate himself from contentions; but all fools mix themselves in quarrels. Because of the cold, the lazy man refuses to plow; therefore he shall beg in summer, and it shall not be given to him. As deep water, so is counsel in the heart of a man; but a wise man will draw it out. Many are called merciful men, but who shall find a faithful man? The just man who walks in his simplicity leaves blessed sons after him. The king who sits on the throne of judgment scatters all evil by his glance. Who can say, "My heart is clean; I am pure from sin"? Diverse weights and diverse measures — both are abominable before God. A child is known by his pursuits, whether his works be pure and right. The ear that hears and the eye that sees — the Lord has made both. Do not love sleep, lest poverty oppress you; open your eyes and be satisfied with bread. "It is bad, it is bad," says every buyer; but when he has gone away, then he will boast. There is gold and a multitude of jewels, but precious lips are a vessel of knowledge. Take the garment of him who has been surety for a stranger, and take a pledge from him for foreigners. Bread of deceit is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth shall be filled with gravel. Thoughts are strengthened by counsel, and...

[Second column, continuing:]
...with wise direction wars are conducted. He who reveals secrets and walks deceitfully and enlarges his lips, do not mingle with him. Whoever curses his father and his mother, his lamp shall be extinguished in the midst of darkness. An inheritance gotten hastily in the beginning shall lack a blessing in the end. Do not say, "I will return evil for evil"; wait for the Lord, and he will deliver you. Diverse weights are an abomination to the Lord, and a false balance is not good. The steps of a man are directed by the Lord; but how can a man understand his own way? It is ruin for a man to devour the holy things, and after vows to retract them. A wise king scatters the wicked, and bends the arch over them. The lamp of the Lord is the breath of man, which searches all the secrets of the belly. Mercy and truth preserve the king, and his throne is strengthened by clemency. The glory of young men is their strength, and the dignity of old men is their gray hair. The bruises of a wound cleanse away evil, and blows that reach the inner parts of the belly. Chapter 21.

As the divisions of waters, so is the heart of the king in the hand of the Lord; whithersoever he will, he shall turn it. Every way of a man seems right to himself, but the Lord weighs the hearts. To do mercy and judgment pleases the Lord more than sacrifices. Haughtiness of the eyes is the enlargement of the heart; the lamp of the wicked is sin. The thoughts of the diligent always tend to abundance, but everyone that is slothful is always in want. He who gathers treasures by a lying tongue is vain and foolish, and shall stumble into the snares of death. The plunder of the wicked shall drag them down, because they refused to do judgment. The way of a wicked man is perverse and strange, but the work of him that is pure is right. It is better to dwell in a corner of the housetop than with a quarrelsome woman in a common house.

results.translation:
[Book] of Proverbs.

The soul of the wicked desires evil: he will not have pity on his neighbor. When the pestilent man is punished, the simple will become wiser; and if he takes heed of the wise, he will gain knowledge. The just man considers the house of the wicked, that he may draw the wicked away from evil. He that stops his ear against the cry of the poor shall also cry himself, and shall not be heard. A gift given secretly extinguishes anger, and a bribe in the bosom the greatest indignation. It is joy to the just to do judgment; and dread to them that work iniquity. The man who wanders out of the way of doctrine shall dwell in the company of giants. He who loves feasting shall be in poverty; he who loves wine and rich food shall not become rich. The wicked shall be given for the just, and the transgressor for the righteous. It is better to dwell in a wilderness than with a contentious and angry woman. A desirable treasure and oil are in the dwelling of the just, but the foolish man shall waste it. He who follows justice and mercy shall find life, justice, and glory. The wise man scales the city of the mighty and pulls down the strength of its confidence. He who guards his mouth and his tongue keeps his soul from troubles. The proud and arrogant is called ignorant; he who acts in anger works pride. Desires kill the slothful, for his hands refuse to work. He covets and desires all day long, but the just man gives and does not cease. The sacrifices of the wicked are abominable, because they are offered from wickedness. A false witness shall perish; the obedient man shall speak of victory. The wicked man impudently hardens his face; but he who is upright corrects his way. There is no wisdom, no prudence, no counsel against the Lord. The horse is prepared for the day of battle, but the Lord grants salvation. Chapter 22.

A good name is better than great riches; good favor is above silver and gold. The rich and the poor have met one another: the Lord is the maker of both. The clever man sees evil and hides himself; the innocent passes on and is afflicted with loss. The reward of humility is the fear of the Lord: riches, glory, and life. Weapons and swords are in the way of the slothful, but he who guards his soul withdraws far from them. It is a proverb: a young man according to his way; even when he is old he will not depart from it. The rich rules over the poor, and he who borrows is servant to the lender. He who sows iniquity shall reap evils, and shall be consumed by the rod of his fury. He who is inclined to mercy shall be blessed, for he has given of his bread to the poor. He who gives gifts shall gain victory and honor, but he takes away the soul of those who receive them. Cast out the scorner and strife shall go out with him, and causes and reproaches shall cease. He who loves cleanness of heart, for the grace of his lips, shall have the king as friend. The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge, and overthrow the words of the wicked. The slothful says, 'A lion is outside; I shall be slain in the midst of the streets.' The mouth of a strange woman is a deep pit; he with whom the Lord is angry shall fall into it. Folly is bound in the heart of a child, and the rod of discipline shall drive it far from him. He who slanders the poor to increase his riches shall himself give to the richer and shall become needy. My son, incline your ear and hear the words of the wise; and apply your heart to my doctrine, which shall be beautiful for you if you keep it in your inmost being; and it shall overflow in your lips, so that your trust may be in the Lord. Therefore I have shown it to you this day. OF PROVERBS
...a slippery mouth works ruins. Chapter 27.
Boast not of tomorrow: for you know not
what the coming day may bring forth.
Let another praise you, and not your own mouth: a stranger,
and not your own lips. Heavy is a stone and burdensome
is sand: but the wrath of a fool is heavier than both.
Wrath has no mercy: nor sudden
fury; and the onset of a stirred-up spirit
who can bear? Better is open
rebuke than hidden love. Better are
the wounds of one who loves than the deceitful
kisses of one who hates. A soul that is full
tramples upon the honeycomb: but to a hungry soul
even bitter things seem sweet. As a bird
wandering from its nest: so is a man who
abandons his place. With ointment and various
perfumes the heart is delighted: and by the good
counsels of a friend the soul is sweetened.
Do not forsake your own friend, nor your father's friend:
and do not go into your brother's house
in the day of your affliction. Better is a neighbor near
than a brother far off. Study wisdom, my son,
and gladden my heart, that you may be able to answer
one who reproaches you with a word. The astute man,
seeing evil, hides himself: the simple pass on
and suffer loss. Take the garment
of him who has given surety for a stranger: and for
aliens take a pledge from him. Whoever blesses
his neighbor with a loud voice, rising early in the morning,
shall be reckoned as one who curses. A dripping roof
in a day of cold, and a quarrelsome
woman, are alike. He who restrains her
is as one who would hold the wind, or
would pour oil from his right hand. Iron sharpens
iron: and a man sharpens
the countenance of his friend. Whoever tends a fig tree
shall eat its fruit: and he who is guardian of his lord
shall be honored. As in water
face answers to face looking in it: so the hearts of
men are revealed to the prudent.
Hell and destruction are never
filled: likewise the eyes of men are insatiable.
As silver is tried in the crucible
and gold in the furnace: so a man is tried
by the mouth of one who praises him. The heart of the wicked seeks
evil things: but the upright heart seeks knowledge.
If you should pound a fool in a mortar, as barley
is beaten with a pestle: his folly would not
be taken from him. Diligently know
the countenance of your flock: and consider well
your herds. For you shall not have power
forever: but a crown shall be given to you for generation
after generation. The meadows are ready
and the green herbs have appeared: and the hay
is gathered from the mountains. The lambs are for
your clothing: and the goats for the price of a field.
Let the goats' milk be sufficient for your food
and for the necessities of your household: and
for the sustenance of your maidservants. Chapter 28.
The wicked flees though no one pursues:
but the just, like a confident lion,
shall be without fear. For the sins of the land
there are many princes: but through a man of
wisdom and knowledge of these things which they speak, the life
of a ruler shall be prolonged. A poor man who oppresses
the poor is like a violent rain
which brings famine. Those who forsake
the law praise the wicked: those who keep it
contend against them. Evil men do not
understand judgment: but those who seek
the Lord understand all things. Better is
a poor man who walks in his simplicity
than a rich man in perverse ways. He who keeps
the law is a wise son: but he who feeds gluttons
shames his father.
He who gathers riches by usury and unjust
gain, gathers them for the poor.
He who turns away his ear from hearing
the law, his prayer shall be an abomination. He who
leads the righteous astray in an evil way shall fall
into his own ruin: and the innocent shall possess
his goods. A rich man seems wise to himself:
but a poor man of understanding shall search him out.
In the triumph of the righteous there is great glory:
but when the wicked reign, men are ruined.
