...will be lifted up. Many seek the face of a prince: and the judgment of individuals proceeds from the Lord. The just abhor the wicked man: and the wicked abhor those who are in the right way. A son who keeps the word will be free of ruin. Chapter 30.
The words of the Gatherer, the son of Vomiter [Agur, son of Jakeh]. The vision which the man spoke, with whom is God: and who, God remaining with him, was strengthened, said: I am the most foolish of men, and the wisdom of men is not with me. I have not learned wisdom, and I have not known the knowledge of the saints. Who has ascended into heaven and descended? Who has held the spirit in his hands? Who has bound the waters as in a garment? Who has raised up all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is the name of his son, if you know? Every word of God is fire-tried: he is a shield to all who hope in him. Add nothing to his words, lest you be reproved, and found a liar. Two things I have asked of you: deny me not before I die. Remove vanity and lying words far from me. Give me neither beggary nor riches; give me only necessities for my sustenance: lest, being full, I be enticed to deny you and say, Who is the Lord? or being compelled by want, I steal, and perjure the name of my God. Do not accuse a servant to his master, lest he curse you and you fall. There is a generation that curses its father, and does not bless its mother. There is a generation that seems clean to itself, and yet is not washed from its filthiness. There is a generation whose eyes are lofty, and their eyelids lifted up. There is a generation that has swords for teeth, and grinds with its jaw-teeth, to devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men. The leech has two daughters, saying, Bring, bring. There are three things that are never satisfied, and a fourth that never says, Enough: Hell, and the mouth of the womb, and the earth that is never satisfied with water; and fire never says, Enough. The eye that mocks its father, and that despises the labor of its mother in bearing it: let the ravens of the valleys pick it out, and the young eagles eat it. Three things are too wonderful for me, and a fourth I do not know at all: the way of an eagle in the sky, the way of a serpent upon a rock, the way of a ship in the midst of the sea, and the way of a man in his youth. Such also is the way of an adulterous woman, who eats and wipes her mouth, and says, I have done no evil. Under three things the earth trembles, and a fourth it cannot bear: a servant when he reigns, a fool when he is filled with food, an odious woman when she is taken in marriage, and a handmaid when she becomes heir to her mistress. There are four things that are least on earth, and they are wiser than the wise: the ants, a feeble folk, that prepare their food in harvest; the hare, a people not strong, that makes its dwelling in the rock; the locust has no king, yet all of them go forth in bands; the spider clings with its hands, and dwells in the palaces of kings. There are three things that walk well, and a fourth that goes gracefully: the lion, strongest of beasts, who is afraid at the approach of none; the cock girded about the loins, and the ram: and there is no king who can resist him; and he who appears a fool after he has been raised on high. If anyone had understood, he would have laid his hand upon his mouth. He who forcefully presses the udders, to draw forth milk, presses out butter; and he who wrings his nose violently, brings forth blood; and he who provokes anger, brings forth discord.
The words of King Lemuel. Chapter 31.
The vision by which his mother instructed him. What, my beloved? What, beloved of my womb? What, beloved of my vows? Give not your strength to women, nor your riches to destroy kings. Give not to kings, O Lemuel, give not to kings...

...if the net has become dull and blunted—not as before, but grown weak—it must be sharpened with much labor: and wisdom will follow diligence. If a serpent bites in silence, he who slanders secretly is no better off. The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious, but the lips of a fool will swallow him up. The beginning of his words is folly, and the end of his talk is wicked madness. A fool multiplies words. Man does not know what has been before him, and who can tell him what shall come after? The labor of fools wears them out, for they do not know how to go to the city. Woe to you, land whose king is a child, and whose princes feast in the morning! Blessed is the land whose king is nobly born, and whose princes eat at the proper time, for refreshment and not for excess. Through laziness the roof beams sink, and through idle hands the house leaks. Bread is made for laughter, and wine makes life merry, and money answers everything. Do not curse the king even in your thought, and do not curse the rich man in your bedchamber, for a bird of the air may carry your voice, and a winged creature may report what you say.

Chapter 11. Cast your bread upon the waters, for after many days you will find it again. Give a portion to seven, and also to eight, for you do not know what evil may come upon the earth. If the clouds are full, they will pour out rain upon the earth. If a tree falls to the south or to the north, wherever it falls, there it shall lie. He who watches the wind will not sow, and he who regards the clouds will never reap. As you do not know the way of the spirit, or how the bones grow in the womb of a woman with child, so you do not know the work of God, who makes all things. In the morning sow your seed, and in the evening let not your hand be idle, for you do not know which will prosper, this or that, or whether both alike will be good. Light is sweet, and it is pleasant for the eyes to see the sun.

If a man lives many years and rejoices in them all, he should remember the days of darkness, for they will be many; when they come, all that has gone before will be shown to be vanity. Rejoice, therefore, young man, in your youth, and let your heart be glad in the days of your youth; walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.

Wisdom.

[Continuing a discourse on the Israelites in the wilderness, contrasting them with the Egyptians:] They had leaders on unknown ways, and you gave them a sun without harm as a good guide. Those [Egyptians] indeed deserved to be deprived of light and to suffer imprisonment in darkness, who kept your sons imprisoned, through whom the incorruptible light of the law was to be given to the world. While they were plotting to kill the infants of the righteous, and one child having been exposed was saved, you took away the multitude of their children as punishment, and destroyed them together in the mighty waters. For that night was known beforehand by our fathers, so that knowing surely by what oaths they had believed, they might take courage. Your people therefore received both the salvation of the just and the destruction of the unjust. For as you punished our adversaries, so also calling us to yourself, you glorified us. For the righteous children were secretly sacrificing, and with one accord established the divine law, that they would share alike in the good things and dangers, having already begun to sing the praises of the fathers. But the discordant cry of the enemies echoed back, and the pitiful lament of the wailing infants was heard. The servant was punished with the same penalty as the master, and the common man suffered like the king. Thus all alike had countless dead under one name of death. For the living were not sufficient even to bury them, since in one moment the most precious nation among them was destroyed. For, disbelieving in all things because of the wonders they had seen, when it came time for the destruction of the firstborn indiscriminately, they confessed the people to be of God. For while a peaceful silence enveloped all things and night was in the midst of its swift course, your all-powerful word, O Lord, leapt down from heaven, from the royal throne, a stern warrior into the midst of the doomed land, bearing the sharp sword of your unfeigned command, and stood and filled all things with death; and while standing on the earth, it touched heaven. Then immediately the visions of dreadful dreams greatly troubled them, and fears came unforeseen. And one thrown here, another there, half dead, showed the cause of his death. For the dreams that troubled them made this known beforehand, lest they should perish not knowing why they suffered these evils. And the trial of death touched also the just, and a plague came in the wilderness upon the multitude, but your wrath did not last long. For a man without complaint hastened to intercede for the people, bringing forward the shield of his own service, prayer and propitiation through incense; he withstood the wrath and put an end to it, showing that he was your servant. He overcame the raging crowd not by strength of body, nor by force of arms, but by his word he subdued him who tormented, calling to mind the oaths and covenant made with the fathers. For when the dead already lay in heaps upon one another, he stood in the midst and stopped the wrath, and cut off the way that was leading to the living. For upon his long robe was the whole world depicted, and the glories of the fathers were engraved on the four rows of stones, and your majesty was written upon the diadem of his head. To these the destroyer yielded, and feared them, for the trial of wrath alone was sufficient. Chapter XIX.

But upon the wicked wrath came without mercy to the very end, for God knew beforehand even their future doings: that having let the Israelites go, and having urged them with great earnestness to depart, they would repent and pursue them. For while they were still mourning and lamenting at the graves of their dead, they conceived another foolish plan, and pursued as fugitives those whom they had driven out with entreaties. For a deserved necessity brought them to this end, and made them forget the things that had happened to them.

For every creature was refashioned again according to its kind from the beginning, obeying Your commandments, so that Your children might be kept unharmed. For a cloud overshadowed their camp, and where water had been before, dry land appeared, and out of the Red Sea a way without hindrance, and a field springing up out of the great deep, through which the whole nation passed which was covered by Your hand. You showed Your marvels and wonders. For like horses they fed on food, and like lambs they exulted, magnifying You, O Lord, who delivered them. For they still remembered the things that had happened during their sojourn, how instead of the birth of animals the land brought forth flies, and how the river vomited forth a multitude of frogs, and yet, at the last, they saw a new creation of birds when, led on by desire, they demanded feasts of delicacies. For in the calling of their desire, a quail rose to them from the sea; and torments came upon sinners, not without those signs which had been made beforehand through the violence of the rivers. For they suffered justly according to their own wickedness. They increased in inhospitality... others admitted foreigners; others reduced good guests to servitude. [Prologue of Ecclesiasticus, right column, red heading:]
'Here begins the Prologue of the book of Jesus, son of Sirach, called Ecclesiasticus.'

Many and great things have been given to us through the Law and the Prophets and the others who followed them, for which Israel ought to be praised for instruction and wisdom's sake; because it is necessary not only that the readers themselves become skilled, but also that those studying from outside may be able, both by speaking and writing, to become most learned. My grandfather Jesus, after he had given himself much to the diligent reading of the Law and the Prophets and other books which had been handed down to us by our forefathers, and had himself acquired considerable proficiency in them, was moved to write something himself pertaining to instruction and wisdom, so that those who are eager to learn, and become conformed to a lawful life, might make greater and greater progress in mind. I exhort you, therefore, to come with goodwill and attentive study to reading, and to have forgiveness in those things wherein, although we tried diligently to interpret, we may in some particular passages have fallen short in the composition of words. For words in Hebrew have not the same force when translated into another tongue. And not only this book, but even the Law itself, and the Prophets, and the rest of the books, differ not a little from the original.

Omnis iniurie proximi ne memineris: et nichil agas in operibus iniurie. Odibilis coram deo est et hominibus superbia: et execrabilis omnis iniquitas gentium. Regnum a gente in gentem transfertur propter iniustitias et iniurias et contumelias et diversos dolos. Avaro autem nichil est scelestius. Quid superbit terra et cinis? Nichil est iniquius quam amare pecuniam. Hic enim et animam suam venalem habet: quoniam in vita sua proiecit intima sua. Omnis potestas brevis vita: languor prolixior gravat

medicum: Brevem languorem precidit medicus; sic et rex hodie est: et cras morietur. Cum enim morietur homo: hereditabit serpentes et bestias et vermes. Initium superbie hominis apostatare a deo: quoniam ab eo qui fecit illum recessit cor eius: quoniam initium peccati est omnis superbia. Qui tenuerit illam adimplebitur maledictis: et subvertet eum in finem. Propterea exhonoravit dominus conventus malorum: et destruxit eos usque in finem. Sedes ducum superborum destruxit deus: et sedere fecit mites pro eis. Radices gentium superbarum arefecit deus: et plantavit humiles ex ipsis gentibus. Terras gentium evertit dominus: et perdidit eas usque ad fundamentum. Arefecit ex ipsis et dispersit eos: et cessare fecit memoriam eorum a terra. Memoriam superborum perdidit deus: et reliquit memoriam humilium sensu. Non est creata hominibus superbia: neque iracundia nationi mulierum. Semen hominum honorabitur hoc quod timet deum: semen autem hoc exhonorabitur quod preterit mandata domini. In medio fratrum rector illorum in honore: et qui timet dominum erunt in oculis illius. Gloria divitum honoratorum et pauperum timor dei est: non despicere hominem iustum pauperem: et non magnificare virum peccatorem divitem. Magnus est iudex et potens in honore: et non est maior illo qui timet deum. Servo sensato liberi servient: et vir prudens et disciplinatus non murmurabit correptus: et inscius non honorabitur. Noli extollere te in faciendo opere tuo: et noli cunctari in tempore angustie. Melior est qui operatur et abundat in omnibus: quam qui gloriatur et eget pane. Fili in mansuetudine serva animam tuam: et da illi honorem secundum meritum suum. Peccantem in animam suam

Know that you walk in the midst of snares, and that you go upon the arms of a battle troubled. According to your strength beware of your neighbor, and treat with the wise and prudent. Let just men be your guests, and let your glory be in the fear of God, and let your thought be on the law of the Most High, and let all your speech be in his commandments. Works shall be praised for the hand of the artisan, and the prince of the people for the wisdom of his speech, but the word of the elders for their good sense. A man full of tongue is terrible in his own city, and he that is rash in his word shall be hateful. Chapter 10. A wise judge shall judge his people, and the government of a man of sense shall be steady. As the judge of the people is himself, so also are his ministers; and what manner of man the ruler of a city is, such also are they that dwell therein. An unwise king shall ruin his people, and cities shall be inhabited through the sense of the prudent. The power of the earth is in the hand of God, and in time he will raise up a profitable ruler over it. The prosperity of man is in the hand of God, and he shall put his glory upon the person of the scribe. Do not remember all the wrongs of your neighbor, and do nothing in the works of injury. Pride is hateful before God and men, and all iniquity of the nations is execrable. A kingdom is translated from one people to another because of injustices and wrongs and injuries and various deceits. There is not a more wicked thing than to love money. Why is earth and ashes proud? There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man, for such a one sets even his own soul to sale, because while he lives he has cast away his innermost things. All power is of short life; a lingering sickness is grievous to the physician; a physician cuts off a short sickness: so a king today is, and tomorrow he shall die. For when a man is dead, he shall inherit serpents and beasts and worms. The beginning of the pride of man is to fall off from God, because his heart is departed from him that made him; for pride is the beginning of all sin. He that holds it shall be filled with maledictions, and it shall ruin him in the end. Therefore the Lord has disgraced the assemblies of the wicked, and has utterly destroyed them. God has overturned the thrones of proud princes, and has set up the meek in their stead. God has dried up the roots of proud nations, and has planted the humble of these nations. The Lord has overturned the lands of the nations, and has destroyed them even to the foundation. He has dried up some of them, and has destroyed them, and has made the memory of them to cease from the earth. God has destroyed the memory of the proud, and has preserved the memory of the humble in mind. Pride was not made for men, nor wrath for the race of women. That seed of men shall be honored which fears God; but that seed shall be dishonored which transgresses the commandments of the Lord. Among brethren, he that is chief is honorable; so shall they that fear the Lord be in his eyes. The glory of the rich, of the honorable, and of the poor is the fear of God: it is not to despise a poor man that is just, and not to magnify a rich man that is a sinner. He is a great man who is a judge and powerful in honor, yet there is none greater than he that fears God. Free men shall serve a wise servant, and a man that is prudent and well instructed will not murmur when he is reproved, and he that is ignorant shall not be honored. Do not extol yourself in doing your work, and do not linger in the time of distress. Better is he that works and abounds in all things than he that boasts himself and wants bread. My son, keep your soul in meekness, and give it honor according to its desert. Who shall justify him that sins against his own soul,

Ecclesiasticus.

...you send it upon his mind and he will keep the words you speak; and he will not spare from malice and from vices. Take heed to yourself and attend diligently to your hearing, for you walk in danger with your gain. But you will hear those words as if in dreams; you will watch over your whole life. Love God and call upon him for your salvation. Every animal loves what is like itself; so too every man loves his neighbor. All flesh joins with what is like itself, and every man will associate with his own kind. How can a wolf ever have fellowship with a lamb? So it is with the sinner and the just. What fellowship has a holy man with a dog, or what portion has a rich man with the poor? The hunting of the lion is the wild ass in the wilderness; so too the poor are the pasture of the rich. And as humility is an abomination to the proud, so is the poor man's disgust hateful to the rich. A rich man wavering is strengthened by his friends; but when the humble man falls, he is driven away even by his acquaintances. When a rich man is deceived, he has many helpers; he speaks proud words, and they justify him. When a humble man is deceived, he is further blamed and argued against. He speaks sensibly, and no place is given to him. A rich man speaks and all fall silent, and they extol his word up to the clouds. A poor man speaks, and they say, 'Who is this?' And if he stumbles, they will overturn him. Good is the substance in which there is no sin of conscience, and most wretched is poverty in the mouth of the impious. The heart of man changes his countenance, whether for good or for evil. It is hard to find, and only with labor, the trace of a good heart and a good face. Chapter 14.

Blessed is the man who has not slipped in word from his mouth, and who is not pricked by the sorrow of sin. Happy is he who has not had sorrow of mind, and has not fallen from his hope. To the greedy and grasping man without reason belongs wealth; and to the envious man, what good is it? He who gathers unjustly for himself, gathers for others; and another will revel in his goods. He who is wicked to himself, to whom will he be good? And he will not rejoice in his own goods. He who envies himself, nothing is worse than he, and this is the reward of his malice. Even if he does good, he does it unknowingly and unwillingly, and in the end his malice is revealed. Evil is the envious eye, that turns away its face and despises its own soul. The insatiable eye of the greedy man in the portion of iniquity will not be satisfied, until it consumes and dries up his own soul. An evil eye looks upon evil things, and will not be satisfied with bread, but remains in need, and will be in sorrow above his own table. Son, if you have anything, do good to yourself, and offer worthy oblations to God. Remember that death does not delay, and that the covenant of the grave has been shown to you. For the covenant of this world surely dies with death. Before death, do good to your friend, and according to your ability, stretch out your hand and give to the poor. Do not defraud yourself of a good day, and let not your share of a good day pass you by. Do not leave to others your sorrows and labors. In the division of your lot, give and receive, and justify your soul. Before your death, work righteousness, for there is no finding of food among the dead. All flesh grows old like grass, and like a leaf that flourishes on a green tree — one is generated while another falls; so is the generation of flesh and blood: one ends, and another is born. Every corruptible work will fail in the end, and he who does it will go with it. But every chosen work will be justified, and he who works it will be honored in it. Blessed is the man who dwells in wisdom, and meditates in righteousness, and in his mind considers the providence of God, who thinks upon its ways in his heart, and understands its hidden things: he shall go forth...

post illam quasi investigator: et in viis illius consistens. Qui respicit per fenestras ilius: et in ianuis illius audiet. Qui requiescit iuxta domum illius: et in parietibus illius figens palum. Statuet casulam suam ad manus illius: et requiescet in casula illius bona per evum. Statuet filios suos sub regimine illius: et sub ramis illius morabitur. Protegetur sub regimine illius a fervore: et in gloria eius requiescet. ca. rv.

Qui timet deum faciet bona: et qui continens est iusticie apprehendet illam: et obviabit illi quasi mater honorificata: et quasi mulier a virginitate suscipiet illum. Cibabit illum pane vite et intellectus: et aqua sapientie salutaris potabit illum. Et firmabitur in illo et non flectetur: et continebit illum et non confundetur: et exaltabit illum apud proximos suos. Et in medio ecclesie aperiet os eius: et adimplebit illum spiritu sapientie et intellectus: et stola glorie vestiet eum. Iocunditatem et exultationem thesaurizabit super illum: et nomine eterno hereditabit illum. Homines stulti non apprehendent illam: et homines sensati obviabunt illi. Homines stulti non videbunt eam: longe enim abest a superbia et dolo. Viri mendaces non erunt illius memores: et viri veraces invenientur in illa: et successum habebunt usque ad inspectionem dei. Non est speciosa laus in ore peccatoris: quoniam a deo profecta est sapientia. Sapientie enim dei astabit laus: et in ore fideli abundabit: et dominator dabit eam illi. Non dixeris: p(rop)ter deum abest: quae enim odit ne feceris. Non dicas illi: ne implanavit: non enim necessarii sunt ei homines impii. Omne execramentum erroris odit dominus: et non erit amabile timentibus eum. Deus ab initio constituit

hominem: et reliquit illum in manu consilii sui. Adiecit mandata et precepta sua. Si volueris mandata conservare: te et in perpetuum fidem placitam facere. Apposuit tibi aquam et ignem: ad quod volueris porrige manum tuam. Ante hominem vita et mors: bonum et malum. Quod placuerit ei dabitur illi: quoniam multa sapientia dei et fortis in potentia: videns omnes sine intermissione. Oculi domini ad timentes eum: et ipse agnoscit omne opera hominis. Nemini mandavit impie agere: et nemini dedit spacium peccandi. Non enim concupiscit multitudinem filiorum infidelium et inutilium. c. xvi.

De iocunderis in filiis impiis si multiplicentur; non oblecteris super ipsos si non est timor dei in illis. Non credas vite illorum: nec respiceris in labores eorum. Melior est enim unus timens deum: quam mille filii impii. Et utile est mori sine filiis: quam relinquere filios impios. Ab uno sensato inhabitabitur patria: et a tribus impiis deseretur. Multa talia vidit oculus meus: et fortiora horum audivit auris mea. In synagoga peccantium exardebit ignis: et in gente incredibili exardescet ira. Non exoraverunt pro peccatis suis antiqui gigantes qui destructi sunt confidentes sue virtuti: et non pepercit peregrinationi illorum, sed percussit eos: et execratus est eos propter superbiam ubi illorum. Non misertus est illis totam gentem perdens: et extollentes se in peccatis suis. Et sicut sexcenta milia peditum qui congregati sunt in duricia cordis sui: et si unus fuisset cervicatus mirum si fuisset immunis. Misericordia enim et ira est cum illo, potens exoratio et effundens iram: secundum misericordiam suam: sic correptio illius, hominem secundum opera

[Continuing on Wisdom] ...after her as an investigator, and stationing oneself in her ways. He that looks through her windows, and listens at her doors. He that lodges near her house, and fixes a stake in her walls. He shall pitch his tent near her, and shall dwell in her good dwelling forever. He shall place his children under her protection, and shall abide under her branches. He shall be protected under her covering from the heat, and shall rest in her glory. [Chapter 15]

He who fears God will do good; and he who holds fast to justice shall obtain her, and she shall meet him as an honored mother, and as a wife of virginity she shall receive him. She shall feed him with the bread of life and understanding, and give him to drink the water of wholesome wisdom. He shall be established in her and shall not be moved, and he shall hold her fast and shall not be confounded, and she shall exalt him among his neighbors. She shall open his mouth in the midst of the assembly, and fill him with the spirit of wisdom and understanding, and clothe him with a robe of glory. She shall lay up joy and gladness upon him, and give him an everlasting inheritance. Foolish men shall not attain her, and men of sense shall meet her. Foolish men shall not see her, for she is far from pride and deceit. Lying men shall not remember her, but truthful men shall be found in her, and shall prosper even to the inspection of God. Praise is not comely in the mouth of a sinner, for wisdom comes forth from God. For the praise of God's wisdom shall stand, and it shall abound in the mouth of the faithful, and the Ruler shall give it to him. Do not say: it is because of God that it is absent; for what He hates, do not do. Do not say to Him: He led me astray; for He has no need of wicked men. The Lord hates every abomination of error, and it shall not be lovable to those who fear Him. God from the beginning created man,

and left him in the hand of his own counsel. He added His commandments and precepts. If you will keep the commandments, they shall preserve you, and forever make faithful acceptance for you. He has set before you water and fire; stretch out your hand to whichever you will. Before man is life and death, good and evil; whichever he chooses shall be given him. For the wisdom of God is great, and He is mighty in power, beholding all things without ceasing. The eyes of the Lord are upon those who fear Him, and He Himself knows every work of man. He has commanded no man to act wickedly, and has given no one license to sin. For He does not desire a multitude of unfaithful and useless children. [Chapter 16]

Do not rejoice in ungodly children, if they multiply; do not delight in them, if the fear of God is not in them. Do not trust their life, nor look upon their labors. For better is one who fears God than a thousand wicked children. And it is better to die without children than to leave behind wicked children. Through one man of understanding a city shall be inhabited, but through the wicked it shall be deserted. My eye has seen many such things, and my ear has heard things stronger still. In the assembly of sinners fire shall be kindled, and wrath shall burn in an unbelieving nation. The ancient giants did not entreat forgiveness for their sins, trusting in their own strength, and were destroyed; nor did He spare the place of their sojourning, but struck them down, and cursed them for their pride there. He did not have mercy on that whole people, destroying them, exalting themselves in their sins. And likewise six hundred thousand footmen who were gathered in the hardness of their heart—had even one been stubborn, it would be a wonder if he were spared. For mercy and wrath are with Him, powerful to forgive and to pour out wrath; according to His mercy, so is His correction of man, according to his works.

results.translation: This page (headed 'Ecclesiasticus') continues the Vulgate Latin text of the Book of Ecclesiasticus (Sirach), spanning roughly the end of chapter 19 and the beginning of chapter 20. The passage warns against yielding to one's own desires and appetites, cautions against drunkenness and the company of loose women which corrupt even the wise, and warns that the wicked will be requited with corruption and shame. It counsels rebuking a friend gently and privately, not to reveal another's faults or betray secrets, and to be slow to believe every word spoken against a neighbor, since a harsh word wounds like an arrow. It teaches that fear of the Lord is the beginning and disposition of all wisdom, and that there is a kind of foolish humility and false shame that harms rather than helps; a wise man is known by his appearance, his laughter, and his gait. Chapter 20 opens by declaring how much better it is to correct someone than to be angry, and not to hinder one who confesses in prayer; it condemns unjust judgment obtained by force, praises open confession of wrongdoing as a way to escape voluntary sin, and distinguishes the wise man who keeps silence appropriately from the fool who talks presumptuously, noting that a wise man will keep silent until the proper time to speak.

There is progress in evils for an undisciplined man, and its finding is to his detriment. There is a gift that is not useful, and there is a gift whose repayment is double. ...[the discourse continues on] the sense where there is bitterness. The knowledge of the wise will abound like a flood, and his counsel remains like a living fountain. The heart of a fool is like a broken vessel, and it will hold no wisdom at all. Whatever a wise man hears, he will praise and add to it; the wanton man hears it and it will displease him, and he will cast it behind his back. The tale of a fool is like a burden on the road, for grace is found in the lips of the sensible. The mouth of the prudent is sought in the assembly, and they will ponder his words in their hearts. As a ruined house, so is wisdom to a fool; and the words of the unwise are stories without meaning. Doctrine to a fool is like fetters on the feet, and like manacles on the right hand. A fool raises his voice in laughter, but a wise man will scarcely laugh quietly. Wise instruction is like a golden ornament to the prudent, and like a bracelet on the right arm. The foot of a fool is quick into the house of his neighbor; but a skilled man will be abashed before the person of the powerful. A fool will peer into the house from the window; but a man of learning will stand outside. It is the folly of a man to listen at the door, but a prudent man will be grieved by the insult. The lips of the imprudent will tell foolish things, but the words of the prudent are weighed in a balance. In the mouth of fools is their heart; but in the heart of the wise is their mouth. When the wicked man curses the devil, he curses his own soul. A whisperer defiles his own soul and will be hated by all; and he who persists will be hated, but the silent and sensible man will be honored. Chapter 26.

He who throws a stone at mire is a sluggard, and all will speak against him with contempt. He who throws stones on the dung of oxen is a sluggard, and whoever touches it will shake his hand. It is a father's confusion to have an undisciplined son; and a foolish daughter will be his disgrace. A prudent daughter is an inheritance for her husband; for...

...she who brings shame pours reproach upon her parent. And an insolent one confounds both father and husband; he will not be esteemed less by the wicked, but will be dishonored by both alike. Music at a funeral is an ill-timed tale; but scourging and instruction are wisdom at all times. He who teaches a fool is like one who glues together potsherds. He who tells a story to one not listening is like one who wakes a sleeper from deep slumber. He who tells wisdom to a fool speaks as to one sleeping, and at the end of the tale he asks, 'Who is this?' Weep over the dead, for his light has failed; and weep over the fool, for his sense has failed. Weep a little over the dead, for he has found rest; but the wicked life of the wicked is worse than death. Mourning for the dead lasts seven days, but for the fool and the impious, all the days of their life. Do not speak much with a fool, and do not go about with a senseless man. Guard yourself from him, so that you may have no trouble, and not be defiled by his sin. Turn away from him and you will find rest, and you will not be wearied by his foolishness. What is heavier than lead? And what else is its name but 'fool'? Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron are easier to bear than an imprudent and foolish and impious man. As a wooden beam bound into the foundation of a building is not loosened, so a heart strengthened by deliberation of counsel [remains firm]. He will minister among great men, and will appear before rulers; he will pass through the land of foreign peoples. He will test good and evil in all things. He will give his heart to rise early to the Lord who made him, and will pray before the Most High. He will open his mouth in prayer, and will beg for his sins. If the great Lord wills, He will fill him with the spirit of understanding: and he himself will send forth words of wisdom like showers, and will confess to the Lord in prayer. And He himself will direct his counsel and discipline: and he will take counsel in his secret things. He himself will make known the discipline of his doctrine, and will glory in the law of the Lord's covenant. Many will praise his wisdom, and it will never be blotted out forever. His memory will not depart, and his name will be sought from generation to generation. Nations will declare his wisdom, and the assembly will proclaim his praise. If he remains, he will leave behind a name greater than a thousand; and if he rests, it will profit him. I will yet take counsel that I may declare, for I am filled as if with fury. And he says in a voice: Hear me, you divine fruits, and bud like the rose planted by the streams of waters. Give forth fragrance like frankincense. Bloom like flowers, like the lily; give forth fragrance, and put forth leaves in grace, and sing praises together, and bless the Lord in his works. Give glory to his name, and confess to him with the voice of your lips, in songs of the lips and with harps; and so you shall speak in confession: all the works of the Lord are exceedingly good. For at his word the water stood as in a heap, and by the word of his mouth as in a reservoir of waters: because it pleased him according to his command, and there is no lessening in his salvation. The works of all flesh are before him, and nothing is hidden from his eyes. He looks from eternity to eternity, and nothing is wonderful in his sight. There is no saying, 'What is this, or what is that?' for all things will be sought in their season. His blessing will overflow like a river, and as a flood has watered the dry land; so his wrath will inherit the nations that have not sought him. As he turned the waters into dryness, and the earth became parched, and his ways are made straight for their ways, so to sinners are stumbling-blocks in his wrath. Good things were created for the good from the beginning: so also for the wicked, both good and evil. The chief things necessary for the life of man are water, fire, and iron, salt, milk, and bread of flour, honey, and the cluster of the grape, oil, and clothing. All these are for good to the saints: so to the impious and sinners they turn to evil. There are spirits that were created for vengeance, and in their fury they confirm their torments. And in the time of consummation they will pour out their strength, and will satisfy the fury of him who made them. Fire, hail, famine, and death: all these were created for vengeance. The teeth of beasts, and scorpions, and serpents, and the sword taking vengeance on the wicked for destruction. They will feast in his commandments, and will be made ready on earth in time of need, and in their times will not pass beyond the word. Therefore from the beginning I was confirmed, and I took counsel, and I thought, and I left it in writing. All the works of the Lord are good, and every work will supply its need in due time. It cannot be said, 'this is worse than that,' for all things will be approved in their time. And now with all your heart and mouth praise and bless the name of the Lord. c.xl.

Ecclesiasticus.

whether a hundred or a thousand years [have passed]. There is no accusing of life in hell. Loathsome children are the children of sinners: and those who dwell near the houses of the wicked. The children of sinners shall lose their inheritance: and with their seed there shall be perpetual reproach. Children complain of an impious father: because on his account they are in reproach. Woe to you, impious men, who have forsaken the law of the Most High Lord. And if you are born, you shall be born in a curse: and if you die, you shall die in a curse. All things that are from the earth shall return to the earth: so also the wicked shall pass from a curse into destruction. The mourning of men is over their bodies: but the name of the wicked shall be blotted out. Take care of a good name: for this shall remain to you more than a thousand great and precious treasures. A good life has its number of days: but a good name shall remain forever. Preserve discipline in peace, my sons. For hidden wisdom and unseen treasure — what use is either? Better is a man who hides his own foolishness than a man who hides his wisdom. Nevertheless, return to those things which proceed from my mouth. For it is not good to observe every irreverence: nor do all things please all men in faith.

Be ashamed before father and mother of fornication: and before a ruler and a powerful man of lying: before a prince and a judge of crime: before the synagogue and the people of iniquity: before a companion and friend of injustice: before the place where you dwell, of theft: of the truth of God and the covenant: of reclining at meals, of the disgrace of giving and receiving: from those who swear falsely, of silence: from regard of a harlot woman: and of turning away the face from a kinsman. Do not turn your face away from your neighbor: and from taking away a portion and not restoring it. Do not gaze upon another man's wife: nor keep company with his maidservant, nor stand by her bed. Beware of friends concerning reproachful words: and when you have given, do not reproach.

Chapter 41.
Do not repeat a word that you have heard, nor reveal a secret matter: and you shall truly be without confusion: and you will find favor in the sight of all men. Do not be confounded for all these things: nor accept a person so as to sin: concerning the law of the Most High and the covenant, and the judgment to justify the wicked: concerning the word of companions and travelers, and the giving of inheritance to friends: of equality in balance and weight: of the acquisition of many things and few: of corruption in buying and of merchants: and of much discipline of children, and of drawing blood from a very bad servant. Over a wicked woman a good seal is a good thing. Where there are many hands, close [things] up: and whatever you deliver, count and weigh it: write down every giving and receiving. Concerning the discipline of the senseless and the fool, and of elders who are judged by the young, and you shall be learned in all things, and approved in the sight of all men.

A daughter is a secret anxiety to her father, and the care of her takes away sleep: lest perhaps in her youth she become an adulteress, or, having dwelt with a man, become hateful: lest she ever be defiled in her virginity, or be found pregnant in her father's house: lest, having dwelt with a man, she go astray, or else become barren. Keep strict watch over a wanton daughter: lest she make you a reproach to your enemies, a byword in the city and an outcast among the people, and put you to shame before the multitude of the people. Do not look upon any man for his beauty, and do not dwell in the midst of women. For from garments comes the moth, and from a woman comes iniquity.

...and the cypress raised itself on high. In receiving the robe of glory and being clothed in the perfection of virtue, in ascending to the holy altar, he gave glory to the vestment of holiness. In receiving the portions from the hand of the priests, he himself stood beside the altar, and around him was a crown of brothers like a planting of cedar on Mount Lebanon: so did they stand around him like branches of palm, and all the sons of Aaron in their glory. When the offering to the Lord was in their hands before the whole congregation of Israel, and he finished his ministry at the altar, to complete the offering to the Most High King, he stretched forth his hand for the libation and poured out from the blood of the grape. He poured it out at the foundations of the altar as a divine odor to the Most High Prince. Then the sons of Aaron cried out and sounded trumpets of beaten metal, and made a great sound to be heard, as a memorial before God. Then all the people together hastened and fell on their faces upon the ground to worship the Lord their God, and to offer prayers to God Almighty, the Most High. And the singers raised their voices in song, and in the great house a sound full of sweetness was heard. And the people entreated the Lord Most High in prayer until the honor of the Lord was completed, and they finished their duty. Then, coming down, he raised his hands over the whole congregation of the children of Israel, to give glory to God with his lips, and to glory in His name. And he repeated his prayer, wishing to show forth the power of God. And he prayed further to the God of all, who has done great things in all the earth, who has increased our days from our mother's womb, and has dealt with us according to His mercy. May He grant us gladness of heart, and bring peace in our days in Israel for everlasting days: that Israel may believe that God's mercy is with us, that He may deliver us in His days. Two nations my soul hates, and a third is not even a nation whom I would hate: those who dwell on Mount Seir, and the Philistines, and the foolish people who dwell in Shechem. Jesus the son of Sirach of Jerusalem wrote the teaching of wisdom and discipline in this book, having renewed wisdom from his heart. Blessed is he who occupies himself with these good things. He who lays them up in his heart shall be wise always. If anyone does these things, he shall prevail in all things, because the light of God is his footstep.

The Prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach

I will confess to you, Lord and King, and I will praise you, God my savior. I will give thanks to your name, for you have become my helper and protector, and have delivered my body from destruction, from the snare of the wicked tongue, and from the lips of those who work falsehood; and in the sight of those who stood by, you became my helper. And you delivered me, according to the abundance of the mercy of your name, from those roaring, ready to devour, from the hands of those seeking my life, and from the gates of tribulations which surrounded me: from the pressure of the flame which surrounded me, and I was not burned in the midst of the fire. From the depth of the belly of hell, and from an unclean tongue, and from lying speech, from an unjust king, and from an unjust tongue. My soul shall praise the Lord even unto death; and my life was drawing near to the grave beneath. They surrounded me on every side, and there was no one to help. I looked for the help of men, and there was none. I remembered your mercy, O Lord, and your works which are from of old: for you deliver those who wait for you, O Lord, and free them from the hand of the nations. You have exalted my dwelling place upon the earth, and I prayed for deliverance from death imminent. I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that He would not forsake me in the day of my trouble, and in the time of the proud.

He will surely turn violently and toss you like a ball into a large country; there you shall die, and there your glorious chariots shall be the shame of your master's house. But they also have erred through wine, and through drunkenness have gone astray: priest and prophet have erred through drunkenness. They have been swallowed up by wine, they have gone astray through drunkenness; they knew not the seer, they were ignorant of judgment. For all tables are full of vomit and filth, so that there is no more room. Whom shall he teach knowledge? And whom shall he make to understand what he hears? For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people, to whom he said: This is my rest, refresh the weary, and this is my refreshment: and they would not hear. And the word of the Lord shall be to them: command upon command, command upon command, line upon line, line upon line, here a little, and there a little: that they may go and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken. Wherefore hear the word of the Lord, you scornful men, who rule over my people that is in Jerusalem. For you have said: We have made a covenant with death, and with hell we have made a pact. When the overflowing scourge shall pass through, it shall not come upon us, for we have made a lie our hope, and by falsehood we are protected. They lie down together, they shall not rise; they are extinguished, quenched as flax. Do not remember former things, nor consider the things of old. Behold, I do a new thing; now it shall spring forth, shall you not know it? I will make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert. The beasts of the field shall honor me, the dragons and the owls, because I give waters in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen. This people I have formed for myself; they shall show forth my praise. But you have not called upon me, O Jacob; but you have been weary of me, O Israel. You have not brought me the small cattle of your burnt offerings, nor honored me with your sacrifices. I have not caused you to serve with offering,

You have bought me no sweet cane with money, neither have you filled me with the fat of your sacrifices; but you have made me to serve with your sins, you have wearied me with your iniquities. I, even I, am he that blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins. Put me in remembrance, let us plead together; declare, that you may be justified. Your first father sinned, and your interpreters have transgressed against me. Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse, and Israel to reproaches.

Who among you fears the Lord, obedient to the voice of his servant? Who walks in darkness, and has no light? Let him trust in the name of the Lord, and lean upon his God. Behold, all you who kindle a fire, encircled with flames: walk in the light of your fire and in the flames which you have kindled. This has been done to you from my hand; you shall lie down in torments.

Hear me, you who follow what is just, and who seek the Lord. Look to the rock from which you were hewn, and to the hollow of the pit from which you were dug. Look to Abraham your father, and to Sarah who bore you; for I called him alone, and blessed him, and multiplied him. The Lord will therefore comfort Zion, and will comfort all her ruins; he will make her wilderness like a paradise, and her desert like the garden of the Lord. Joy and gladness shall be found in her, thanksgiving and the voice of praise.

Attend to me, my people, and give ear to me, my nation, for a law shall go out from me, and my judgment shall rest as a light to the peoples. My righteousness is near, my salvation has gone forth, and my arms shall judge the peoples. The islands will wait for me, and in my arm they will trust. Lift up your eyes to heaven, and look upon the earth beneath; for the heavens shall vanish like smoke, and the earth shall wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants shall likewise perish; but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness shall not fail.

Hearken to me, you who know justice, my people who have my law in their heart. Do not fear the reproach of men, and be not afraid of their revilings; for the moth shall eat them like a garment, and the worm shall devour them like wool; but my salvation shall be forever, and my righteousness unto all generations.

Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the Lord. Awake as in the days of old, in the generations of long ago. Was it not you who cut Rahab in pieces, and wounded the dragon? Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a way for the redeemed to pass over? So the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come with singing to Zion; and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads. They shall obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

I, I myself, am he who comforts you. Who are you that you should fear mortal man, and the son of man who withers like grass? And you have forgotten the Lord your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth, and you have feared continually all the day because of the fury of the oppressor, as though he were ready to destroy. Where now is the fury of the oppressor? He who is bowed down shall soon be released, and shall not die and go down to the pit, nor shall his bread fail. For I am the Lord your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar; the Lord of hosts is my name. I have put my words in your mouth, and have covered you in the shadow of my hand, that I may plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and say to Zion, You are my people.

Awaken, awaken, rise up, O Jerusalem, who has drunk from the hand of the Lord the cup of his wrath; you have drunk the dregs of the cup of trembling, and drained it to the very dregs. There is none to guide her among all the sons she has brought forth; there is none to take her by the hand among all the sons she has raised. Two things have befallen you—who will grieve for you? Devastation and destruction, famine and sword—who will comfort you? Your sons lay helpless; they lay at the head of every street like an antelope caught in a net, full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of your God.

Jeremiah.

As a cage full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become great and rich; they are grown fat and sleek, and they have passed over my words most wickedly. They have not judged the cause of the widow, nor directed the cause of the fatherless, nor judged the judgment of the poor. Shall I not visit for these things, saith the Lord, or shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this? A wonderful and horrible thing has been done in the land. The prophets prophesied falsehood, and the priests applauded with their hands, and my people loved such things. What then shall be done in the end thereof? Chapter 6.

Gather yourselves together, sons of Benjamin, out of the midst of Jerusalem, and blow the trumpet in Tekoa, and set up a signal over Beth-haccerem, for evil is seen from the north, and great destruction. I have likened the daughter of Zion to a beautiful and delicate woman. Shepherds and their flocks shall come to her. They have pitched their tents against her round about; each one shall feed those who are in his own hand. Sanctify war against her; arise, and let us go up at noon. Woe to us, for the day has declined, for the shadows of the evening are grown longer. Arise, and let us go up by night, and destroy her houses; for thus says the Lord of hosts: Cut down her wood, and cast up a mound around Jerusalem. This is the city of visitation; all oppression is in the midst of her. As a cistern makes its water cold, so has she made her wickedness cold. Iniquity and destruction shall be heard in her continually before me; sickness and wounds. Be instructed, Jerusalem, lest my soul depart from you, lest I make you a desert, an uninhabitable land. Thus says the Lord of hosts: They shall thoroughly glean the remnant of Israel, as in a vineyard; turn back your hand as a grape-gatherer to the basket.

To whom shall I speak, and testify, that they may hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the word of the Lord has become to them a reproach; they will not receive it. Therefore I am full of the fury of the Lord; I am weary with holding it in. Pour it out upon the children in the street, and upon the assembly of young men together; for even the husband with the wife shall be taken, the aged with him who is full of days. And their houses shall pass to others, their fields and wives together; for I will stretch out my hand upon the inhabitants of the land, says the Lord. For from the least even to the greatest, everyone is given to covetousness; and from the prophet even to the priest, everyone deals falsely. They have healed the wound of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace, when there is no peace. They were confounded because they committed abomination; nay, they were not at all confounded, neither could they blush. Therefore they shall fall among those that fall; in the time of their visitation they shall be cast down, says the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Stand in the ways and see, and ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk in it, and you shall find rest for your souls. But they said, We will not walk in it. And I set watchmen over you. And I said, Hearken to the sound of the trumpet. But they said, We will not hearken. Therefore hear, you nations, and know, O congregation, what great things I will do among them. Hear, O earth: behold, I will bring evil upon this people, the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not hearkened to my words, and they have cast away my law. To what purpose does frankincense come to me from Sheba, and the sweet cane from a far country? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, nor your sacrifices pleasing to me. Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will lay stumbling blocks before this people, and the fathers and the sons together shall fall upon them; the neighbor and his friend shall perish.

For among the reproaches of many and the terror round about, you have pursued and let us pursue him: from all the men who were peaceable with me and watching my side. If somehow he may be deceived and we may prevail against him, and we may take vengeance on him for it. But the Lord is with me as a mighty warrior; therefore those who persecute me will stumble and be weak, and they will be greatly confounded, because they did not understand the everlasting reproach that shall never be blotted out. And you, O Lord of hosts, who try the just and see the reins and the heart, let me see your vengeance on them, for to you I have revealed my cause. Sing to the Lord, praise the Lord: for he has delivered the soul of the poor from the hand of evildoers. Cursed be the day on which I was born: let the day on which my mother bore me not be blessed. Cursed be the man who announced to my father saying, a male child is born to you, and made him glad as with joy. Let that man be like the cities which the Lord overthrew and did not repent. Let him hear a cry in the morning and wailing at noon-time, because he did not kill me from the womb, that my mother might have been my grave, and her womb an everlasting conception. Why did I come forth from the womb to see labor and sorrow, and that my days should be consumed in confusion? Chapter 21.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord: when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying: Inquire of the Lord for us, for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon makes war against us: perhaps the Lord will deal with us according to all his wondrous works, and he will withdraw from us. And Jeremiah said to them: Thus you shall say to Zedekiah. Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands
with which you fight against the king of Babylon and the Chaldeans who besiege you around the walls: and I will gather them in the midst of this city. And I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and with a strong arm and in fury and in indignation and in great wrath: and I will strike the inhabitants of this city. Men and beasts shall die of a great pestilence. And afterward, says the Lord, I will give Zedekiah king of Judah and his servants and his people, and those who are left in this city from the pestilence and the sword and the famine, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those seeking their life: and he will strike them with the edge of the sword: he will not spare nor have pity nor show mercy. And to this people you shall say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death. He who remains in this city shall die by sword and famine and pestilence: but he who goes out and flees to the Chaldeans who besiege you shall live, and his life shall be to him as spoil. For I have set my face against this city for evil and not for good, says the Lord. It shall be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he shall burn it with fire, and the house of the king of Judah. Hear the word of the Lord, O house of David. Thus says the Lord: Execute judgment in the morning, and deliver him who is oppressed out of the hand of the oppressor: lest my indignation go forth like fire and burn, and there be none to quench it, because of the evil of your doings. Behold, I am against you, O inhabitant of the valley, and of the rock of the plain, says the Lord: you who say, who shall strike us, and who shall enter our houses? And I will punish you according to the fruit of your doings, says the Lord: and I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it shall devour all things round about her. Chapter 22.

...and there you shall die. And into the land to which they lift up their soul to return, they shall not return. Is this man Jeconiah a despised and broken vessel? Is he a vessel with no pleasure in it? Why are they cast out, he and his seed, and cast into a land which they knew not? O land, land, land, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Write this man down as childless, a man who shall not prosper in his days; for none of his seed shall sit upon the throne of David or rule any more in Judah. Chapter 23.

Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, says the Lord. Therefore thus says the Lord God of Israel concerning the shepherds who feed my people: You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and have not visited them. Behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, says the Lord. And I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all the lands to which I have driven them, and will bring them back to their folds, and they shall grow and multiply. And I will set up shepherds over them who shall feed them; they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall any be lacking, says the Lord. Behold, the days come, says the Lord, when I will raise up unto David a righteous Branch, and a king shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth. In those days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely; and this is the name by which he shall be called: The Lord our Righteousness. Therefore, behold, the days come, says the Lord, when they shall no longer say, 'As the Lord lives who brought up the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt,' but 'As the Lord lives who brought up and led the seed of the house of Israel out of the land of the north, and from all the lands where I had driven them'; and they shall dwell in their own land. Concerning the prophets: My heart is broken within me, all my bones tremble. I have become like a drunken man, like a man overcome with wine, because of the Lord and because of his holy words; for the land is full of adulterers; because of the curse the land mourns, the pastures of the wilderness are dried up. Their course is evil, and their might is not right. For the prophet and the priest are polluted; even in my house I have found their wickedness, says the Lord. Therefore their way shall be to them like slippery paths in darkness; they shall be driven on and shall fall in it, for I will bring evil upon them, the year of their visitation, says the Lord. And in the prophets of Samaria I have seen folly: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray. And in the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: committing adultery and walking in lies; they strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his wickedness. They have all become to me like Sodom, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah. Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the prophets: Behold, I will feed them with wormwood and give them gall to drink; for from the prophets of Jerusalem pollution has gone out into all the land. Thus says the Lord of hosts: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you and deceive you. They speak a vision of their own heart, not from the mouth of the Lord. They say to those who despise me, 'The Lord has spoken: peace shall be yours'; and to everyone who walks in the stubbornness of his own heart they say, 'No evil shall come upon you.' For who has stood in the council of the Lord, and has perceived and heard his word? Who has marked his word and heard it? Behold, a whirlwind of the Lord's indignation shall go forth, and a sweeping tempest shall burst upon the head of the wicked. The anger of the Lord shall not turn back until he has executed and until he has accomplished the thoughts of his heart. In the latter days you shall understand it fully.

Why has he prophesied in the name of the Lord, saying: This house shall be like Shiloh, and this city shall be desolate so that there will be no inhabitant? And all the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the Lord. And when the princes of Judah heard these words, they went up from the king's house to the house of the Lord, and sat at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the Lord. And the priests and the prophets spoke to the princes and to all the people, saying: This man deserves the sentence of death, because he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears. And Jeremiah said to all the princes and to all the people: The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and against this city all the words which you have heard. Now therefore, amend your ways and your doings, and obey the voice of the Lord your God, and the Lord will repent of the evil that he has spoken against you. As for me, behold, I am in your hands; do with me as seems good and right in your eyes. But know for certain that if you kill me, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves and upon this city and its inhabitants; for in truth the Lord has sent me to you, to speak in your ears all these words. Then the princes and all the people said to the priests and to the prophets: This man does not deserve the sentence of death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God. The princes of Judah and the princes of Jerusalem, the eunuchs and priests, and all the people of the land who passed between the divisions of the calf—I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those seeking their life, and their dead bodies shall be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. And the cities of Judah I will make a desolation, without inhabitant. Chapter 35. The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, saying: Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak to them, and bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the chambers, and give them wine to drink. So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and all his sons, and the whole house of the Rechabites, and I brought them into the house of the Lord, to the chamber of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, a man of God, which was near the chamber of the princes, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, keeper of the threshold. And I set before the sons of the house of the Rechabites cups full of wine, and goblets, and said to them, Drink wine. But they answered: We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying: You shall not drink wine, you or your sons, forever. And you shall not build houses, and you shall not sow seed, and you shall not plant vineyards...

[Second column]: ...nor shall you have any, but you shall dwell in tents all your days, that you may live many days upon the face of the land in which you sojourn. So we obeyed the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab our father in all that he commanded us, so that we drink no wine all our days, we and our wives, our sons and our daughters, and we do not build houses to dwell in, and we have no vineyard or field or seed; but we dwell in tents and have obeyed and done according to all that Jonadab our father commanded us. But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, Come, let us go into Jerusalem from before the army of the Chaldeans and from before the army of Syria; and we have dwelt in Jerusalem. Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Go and say to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Will you not receive instruction, to obey my words, says the Lord? The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, which he commanded his sons, that they should not drink wine, have prevailed; and they have not drunk unto this day, because they obeyed the commandment of their father. But I have spoken to you, rising early and speaking, and you have not obeyed me. But to the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your father, and kept all his commandments, and done all that he commanded you; therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: There shall not fail a man of the line of Jonadab the son of Rechab to stand before me forever. Chapter 36.

And it came to pass in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, that this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying: Take a scroll of a book, and write in it all the words that I have spoken to you against Israel and Judah and against all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah even to this day: that perhaps the house of Judah, hearing of all the evil that I intend to do to them, may turn each from his evil way, and I may forgive their iniquity and their sin. So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord which he had spoken to him, in a scroll of a book. And Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying: I am shut up; I cannot go into the house of the Lord. Go therefore, and read from the scroll in which you have written from my mouth the words of the Lord, in the hearing of the people in the house of the Lord on the fast day; and also read in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities. Perhaps their prayer will fall before the Lord, and each will turn from his evil way, for great is the wrath and indignation the Lord has pronounced against this people. And Baruch son of Neriah did according to all that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the scroll the words of the Lord in the house of the Lord. Now it came to pass in the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, in the ninth month, they proclaimed a fast before the Lord for all the people in Jerusalem, and for all the multitude that had come together from the cities of Judah into Jerusalem. Then Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court at the entry of the new gate of the house of the Lord, in the hearing of all the people. And when Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the Lord from the book, he went down to the king's house, to the scribe's chamber: and behold, all the princes were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, and Delaiah son of Shemaiah, and Elnathan son of Achbor, and Gemariah son of Shaphan, and Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the princes. And Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read the book in the hearing of the people. Then all the princes sent to Baruch, Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi, saying: Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people, and come. And when they had heard all the words, they were afraid, one and another, and said to Baruch: We must surely tell the king all these words. And they went in to the king in the courtyard. But they had committed the scroll to the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they reported all the words in the hearing of the king. And the king sent Judi to fetch the scroll: who, taking it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe, read it in the hearing of the king and of all the princes who stood about the king. Now the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, and a hearth full of burning coals was set before him. And when Judi had read three or four leaves, he cut it with the scribe's penknife and cast it into the fire that was upon the hearth, until the whole scroll was consumed by the fire that was in the hearth. And they were not afraid, nor did they tear their garments, the king and all his servants who heard all these words. Nevertheless Elnathan and Delaiah and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the book, but he would not listen to them. And the king commanded Jerahmeel the son of Hammelech, and Seraiah the son of Azriel, and Shelemiah the son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet: but the Lord hid them. And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, after the king had burned the scroll and the words which Baruch had written at the mouth of Jeremiah, saying: Take again another scroll, and write in it all the former words that were in the first scroll which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned. And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah say: Thus says the Lord: You have burned this scroll, saying, Why have you written in it, declaring - the king of Babylon shall surely come and destroy this land, and shall cause man and beast to cease from it? Therefore thus says the Lord... [continuing on right column] ...God against Jehoiakim king of Judah: He shall have none to sit upon the throne of David, and his dead body shall be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night. And I will punish him and his seed and his servants for their iniquities, and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the evil that I have pronounced against them, and they did not listen. Jeremiah, however, took another scroll and gave it to Baruch the son of Neriah the scribe, who wrote in it, from the mouth of Jeremiah, all the words of the book which Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned with fire: and there were added besides many more words like them. And king Zedekiah sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: Pray for us to the Lord our God. Now Jeremiah walked freely among the people, for they had not yet put him into the prison. Then the army of Pharaoh came out of Egypt: and the Chaldeans who besieged Jerusalem, hearing the news, withdrew from Jerusalem. And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, saying: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Thus shall you say to the king of Judah, who sent you to inquire of me: Behold, the army of Pharaoh which has come out to help you shall return to its own land, into Egypt: and the Chaldeans shall come again, and fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire. ...with wild beasts and satyrs, and it shall dwell there desolate. And it shall not be inhabited any more forever, nor shall it be rebuilt from generation to generation. As the Lord overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, says the Lord, no man shall dwell there, nor shall a son of man abide in it. Behold, a people shall come from the north, a great nation, and many kings shall rise from the ends of the earth. They shall take bow and shield; they are cruel and show no mercy. Their voice shall roar like the sea, and they shall ride upon horses, like a man prepared for battle, against you, daughter of Babylon. The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands have grown feeble. Anguish has seized him, pain as of a woman in labor. Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong dwelling place, for I will suddenly make him run away from it. And who is the chosen one whom I shall appoint over it? For who is like me, and who shall stand against me? And who is that shepherd who can withstand my presence? Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord which he has conceived against Babylon, and his purposes which he has purposed against the land of the Chaldeans. Surely the little ones of the flock shall drag them away; surely their habitation shall be destroyed with them. At the sound of the capture of Babylon the earth shall be moved, and the cry shall be heard among the nations.

Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will raise up against Babylon and against the inhabitants of it who have lifted up their heart against me a destroying wind, and I will send winnowers into Babylon who shall winnow her. And they shall destroy her land, for they have come upon her on every side in the day of her affliction. Let not him who bends the bow bend it, nor let him who is armored rise up. Do not spare her young men; destroy all her army. And the slain shall fall in the land of the Chaldeans, wounded in her territories, for Israel and Judah have not been widowed by their God, the Lord of hosts, though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel. Flee from the midst of Babylon, and let every man save his life. Do not be silent about her iniquity, for it is the time of the Lord's vengeance; he will repay her according to her deeds. Babylon has been a golden cup in the hand of the Lord, making all the earth drunk; the nations have drunk of her wine and therefore have gone mad. Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is broken; wail over her, take balm for her pain, if perhaps she may be healed. We tried to heal Babylon, but she is not healed. Let us forsake her, and let each go to his own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens and is lifted up to the clouds. The Lord has brought forth our righteousness: come, let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God. Sharpen the arrows, fill the quivers. The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his purpose against Babylon is to destroy it, for it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple. Set up a signal upon the walls of Babylon; strengthen the watch, station the watchmen, prepare ambushes, for the Lord has both purposed and done what he spoke against the inhabitants of Babylon. O you who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your covetousness. The Lord of hosts has sworn by himself: surely I will fill you with men as with locusts, and they shall raise a shout over you.
