And the word of the LORD came to me, saying: What do you mean, that you use this proverb concerning the land of Israel, saying: The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge? As I live, says the Lord GOD, you shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Israel. Behold, all souls are mine; as the soul of the father, so also the soul of the son is mine: the soul that sins, it shall die. But if a man be just, and do that which is lawful and right, and has not eaten upon the mountains, nor lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, nor defiled his neighbor's wife, nor approached a menstruous woman, nor oppressed anyone, but has restored the debtor's pledge, has robbed none by violence, has given his bread to the hungry, and covered the naked with a garment, has not lent upon usury, nor taken any increase, has withdrawn his hand from iniquity, and executed true judgment between man and man, has walked in my statutes, and kept my judgments, to deal truly - he is just, he shall surely live, says the Lord GOD. If he beget a son who is a robber, a shedder of blood, and who does any of these things (though he himself did none of these things), but instead eats upon the mountains, defiles his neighbor's wife, oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, does not restore the pledge, lifts up his eyes to the idols, commits abomination, gives upon usury, and takes increase: shall he live? He shall not live. Seeing he has done all these detestable things, he shall surely die; his blood shall be upon him. Now if he beget a son who, seeing all his father's sins which he has done, considers, and does not do likewise, does not eat upon the mountains, nor lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, nor defile his neighbor's wife, nor grieve anyone, nor withhold the pledge, nor commit robbery, but has given his bread to the hungry, and covered the naked with a garment, has withdrawn his hand from oppressing the poor, has not received usury or increase, has executed my judgments, and walked in my statutes - he shall not die for the iniquity of his father, he shall surely live. As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, spoiled his brother by violence, and did that which is not good among his people, behold, he shall die in his iniquity. Yet you say, Why does not the son bear the iniquity of the father? Because the son has done that which is lawful and right, and has kept all my statutes, and done them, he shall surely live. The soul that sins, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son: the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him. But if the wicked will turn from all his sins that he has committed, and keep all my statutes, and do that which is lawful and right, he shall surely live, he shall not die. All his transgressions that he has committed, they shall not be remembered against him: in his righteousness that he has done he shall live. Have I any pleasure at all that the wicked should die? says the Lord GOD, and not that he should turn from his ways and live? But when the righteous turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? All his righteousness that he has done shall not be remembered: in his trespass that he has trespassed, and in his sin that he has sinned, in them shall he die. Ezekiel.

[I] will not answer you, neither shall the thought of your mind come to pass, when you say: Let us be as the nations and as the families of the earth, to worship wood and stone. As I live, says the Lord God, with a strong hand and outstretched arm and outpoured wrath I will reign over you. And I will bring you out from the peoples, and gather you out of the lands in which you are scattered, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm and outpoured wrath, I will reign over you, and I will lead you into the wilderness of the peoples, and there I will enter into judgment with you face to face. As I entered into judgment with your fathers in the wilderness of the land of Egypt, so will I judge you, says the Lord. And I will make you pass under the rod, and I will bring you into the bonds of the covenant. And I will separate from you the rebels and the wicked; I will bring them out of the land of their sojourning, but they shall not enter into the land of Israel, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And as for you, house of Israel, thus says the Lord God: Go, every one of you, serve your idols; but afterward, if you do not listen to me, you shall no more profane my holy name with your gifts and your idols. For on my holy mountain, on the high mountain of Israel, says the Lord God, there all the house of Israel shall serve me, all of them, in the land where they shall please me; and there I will require your firstfruits and the choicest of your tithes, with all your sanctified things. I will accept you as a sweet savor when I bring you out from the peoples and gather you from the lands into which you have been scattered, and I will be sanctified in you in the sight of the nations. And you shall know that I am the Lord, when I bring you into the land of Israel, into the land for which I lifted up my hand to give it to your fathers. And there you shall remember your ways and all your deeds by which you have been defiled, and you shall loathe yourselves in your own sight for all the evils which you have done. And you shall know that I am the Lord when I have dealt well with you for my name's sake, not according to your evil ways nor according to your corrupt deeds, O house of Israel, says the Lord God.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face toward the south, and drop your word toward the south wind; and prophesy against the forest of the southern field, and say to the southern forest: Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will kindle a fire in you, and it shall devour every green tree in you and every dry tree; the flame of its kindling shall not be quenched, and every face from the south to the north shall be burned by it. And all flesh shall see that I the Lord have kindled it; it shall not be quenched. And I said: Ah, Lord God! They say of me: Does he not speak in parables?

Chapter 21.

And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, set your face toward Jerusalem, and drop your word toward the sanctuaries, and prophesy against the land of Israel, and say to the land of Israel: Thus says the Lord God: Behold, I am against you, and I will draw my sword out of its sheath, and will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked. Since therefore I will cut off from you the righteous and the wicked, my sword shall go forth out of its sheath against all flesh from south to north, that all flesh may know that I the Lord have drawn my sword out of its sheath; it shall not return. And you, son of man, groan with breaking loins, and groan bitterly before them. And when they say to you, Why do you groan? you shall say: Because of the news that is coming, every heart shall melt, and all hands shall be feeble, and every spirit shall faint, and all knees shall run with water. Behold, it comes, and it shall be done, says the Lord God. And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, prophesy, and say: Thus says the Lord God: Speak.

The sword, the sword is sharpened and polished. That it may slaughter victims it is sharpened: that it may flash it is polished. Who moves the scepter of my son, you have cut down all wood: and I have given it to be smoothed, that it may be held in the hand. This sharpened one is a sword, and this polished one is in the hand of the killer. Cry out and howl, son of man: for this is done in my people, this in all the princes of Israel who have fled. They are delivered to the sword together with my people. Therefore strike upon your thigh, because it is tested: and this shall be even when the scepter is overthrown, and it shall not be, says the Lord God. And you, son of man, prophesy, and strike hand against hand: and let the sword be doubled and the sword of the slain be tripled. This is the sword of great slaughter, which makes them numb and their hearts melt away, and multiplies ruins. At all their gates I have set the terror of the sharpened and polished sword, made ready for flashing, girded for slaughter. Sharpen it, go to the right or to the left, wherever your face is set. I too will clap my hands together and will fulfill my indignation. I the Lord have spoken. And the word of the Lord came to me saying: And you, son of man, appoint for yourself two ways, that the sword of the king of Babylon may come. Both shall go forth from one land. And with his hand he shall take a divination, he shall cast lots at the head of the way of the city. You shall make a way, that the sword may come to Rabbath of the sons of Ammon, and to Judah, into fortified Jerusalem. For the king of Babylon stood at the crossroads, at the head of the two ways, seeking divination, mixing arrows. He inquired of idols, he consulted entrails. In his right hand was the divination for Jerusalem, to set battering rams, to open the mouth in slaughter, to lift up the voice in howling, to set battering rams against the gates, to cast up a mound, to build siege works.

And to them it seems as one consulting an oracle in vain in their eyes, and imitating the rest of sabbaths. But he will call to mind the iniquity to seize them. Therefore thus says the Lord God: Because you have caused your iniquity to be remembered, and your transgressions have been revealed, and your sins have appeared in all your thoughts: because, I say, you have been remembered, you shall be seized by hand. And you, profane and wicked one, prince of Israel, whose day has come in the time of appointed iniquity: thus says the Lord God: Remove the mitre, take off the crown. This shall no longer be as it was; he who was humble shall be exalted, and he who was exalted shall be humbled. I will make it an overthrow, an overthrow, an overthrow: and this shall not be until he comes whose right it is, and I will give it to him. And you, son of man, prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord God concerning the sons of Ammon, and concerning their reproach. And you shall say: A sword, a sword drawn for slaughter, polished to consume and to flash - because you saw false visions and divined lies - to lay you upon the necks of the wicked slain, whose day shall come in the time of appointed iniquity. Return to your sheath, to the place where you were created. In the land of your birth I will judge you, and I will pour out my indignation upon you. I will blow upon you in the fire of my wrath, and I will give you into the hands of brutish men, skilled in destruction. You shall be fuel for the fire. Your blood shall be in the midst of the land; you shall be forgotten: for I the Lord have spoken. Chapter 22.
And the word of the Lord came to me saying: And you, son of man, will you not judge the bloody city, and show her all her abominations? And you shall say: Thus says the Lord God: A city that sheds blood in her midst, that her time may come; and that has made idols against herself to defile herself. In blood

...my [wrath?] consumed them. Now I have brought their way upon their head, says the Lord God. Chapter 23.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying: Son of man, there were two women, daughters of one mother, and they committed fornication in Egypt. In their youth they played the harlot. There their breasts were pressed, and there the bosoms of their virginity were bruised. And their names were: Oholah the elder, and Oholibah her sister the younger. And I took them, and they bore sons and daughters. Now their names: Samaria is Oholah, and Jerusalem is Oholibah.
So Oholah played the harlot against me, and doted on her lovers, the Assyrians who came near her, clothed with hyacinth blue, captains and rulers, desirable young men, all horsemen riding on horses: and she bestowed her harlotries upon them, all of them chosen men of Assyria, and with all in whose filthiness she doted she was defiled. Moreover she did not leave off the fornications she had had in Egypt. For they had lain with her in her youth, and they had bruised the bosom of her virginity, and poured out their fornication upon her.
Therefore I delivered her into the hand of her lovers, into the hand of the sons of Assyria, upon whom she doted with lust. They uncovered her shame, took away her sons and daughters, and slew her with the sword. And she became infamous among women, and they executed judgments upon her.
And when her sister Oholibah saw this, she was more corrupt in her lustful doting than she, and her fornication surpassed the fornication of her sister; she gave herself shamelessly to the sons of Assyria, to captains and rulers who came to her, clothed in varied garments, horsemen riding on horses, and young men all handsome in form. And I saw that both were defiled in the same way, and she increased her fornications. And when she saw men portrayed on the wall,
images of the Chaldeans expressed in colors, girded with belts about their loins, and dyed turbans upon their heads, all of them looking like princes, after the likeness of the sons of Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans, their native land: she doted upon them at the sight of her eyes, and sent messengers to them into Chaldea.
And when the sons of Babylon came to her, into the bed of her breasts, they defiled her with their fornications, and she was defiled by them, and her soul was sated by them. She likewise uncovered her fornications, and exposed her shame.
And my soul departed from her, just as my soul had departed from her sister. For she multiplied her fornications, remembering the days of her youth, in which she had played the harlot in the land of Egypt: and she doted with lust upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is as the issue of horses.
Thus you called to remembrance the wickedness of your youth, when in Egypt your breasts were pressed, and the bosom of your virginity was bruised.
Therefore, O Oholibah, thus says the Lord God: Behold, I will raise up your lovers against you, of whom your soul was sated, and I will gather them against you on every side: the sons of Babylon and all the Chaldeans, the nobles and tyrants and princes, all the sons of Assyria, young men of excellent form, captains and rulers, all of them princes of princes, and renowned horsemen. And they shall come against you equipped with chariot and wheel, and a multitude of peoples. They shall arm themselves against you on every side with breastplate, shield, and helmet. And I will set judgment before them, and they shall judge you according to their judgments.
And I will set my jealousy against you, which they exercised in fury. They shall mutilate your nose and your ears, and what remains shall fall by the sword. They shall take your sons and your daughters, and your remnant

Ezekiel.

[the land] was profaned among the nations, that which you profaned in the midst of them: that the nations may know that I am the Lord, says the Lord of hosts. When I shall be sanctified in you before them. For I will take you from among the nations, and gather you from all the lands, and bring you into your own land. And I will pour clean water upon you, and you shall be cleansed from all your filthiness, and from all your idols I will cleanse you. And I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you. And I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my spirit within you: and I will cause you to walk in my commandments, and to keep my judgments, and do them. And you shall dwell in the land that I gave to your fathers, and you shall be my people, and I will be your God. And I will save you from all your uncleannesses, and I will call for the corn and multiply it, and I will lay no famine upon you. And I will multiply the fruit of the tree and the increase of the field, that you bear no more the reproach of famine among the nations. And you shall remember your evil ways, and your doings that were not good, and your iniquities and your wicked deeds shall displease you in your own sight. Not for your sakes do I do this, says the Lord God, be it known to you. Be ashamed and confounded for your ways, O house of Israel. Thus says the Lord God: In the day when I shall have cleansed you from all your iniquities, and shall cause the cities to be inhabited, and shall repair the ruinous places, and the desolate land shall be tilled, whereas it was waste in the sight of all that passed by: they shall say, This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden; and the wasted and desolate and ruined cities are fortified and inhabited. And the nations that shall be left round about you shall know that I the Lord have built up the ruined places, and planted that which was desolate: I the Lord have spoken it, and I will do it.

Thus says the Lord God: Yet again shall the house of Israel seek me to do this for them. I will multiply them like a flock of men, as a holy flock, as the flock of Jerusalem in her solemn feasts; so shall the waste cities be filled with flocks of men: and they shall know that I am the Lord. Chapter 37.

The hand of the Lord came upon me, and led me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of a plain that was full of bones. And he led me about among them round about, and behold there were very many upon the surface of the plain, and they were very dry. And he said to me: Son of man, do you think these bones shall live? And I said: Lord God, you know. And he said to me: Prophesy over these bones, and say to them: O dry bones, hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord God to these bones: Behold, I will send spirit into you, and you shall live. And I will lay sinews upon you, and will make flesh grow over you, and cover you with skin, and give you spirit, and you shall live, and you shall know that I am the Lord. And I prophesied as he had commanded me. And as I prophesied there was a noise, and behold a shaking, and the bones came together, each bone to its joint. And I saw, and behold sinews and flesh came up upon them, and skin was stretched over them, but there was no breath in them. And he said to me: Prophesy to the spirit, prophesy, son of man, and say to the spirit: Thus says the Lord God: Come from the four winds, O spirit, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live again. So I prophesied as he had commanded me, and the spirit entered into them, and they lived, and they stood up upon their feet, an exceedingly great army. And he said to me: Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel.

...my holy name any more; and the nations shall know that I am the Lord, the Holy One of Israel. Behold it cometh, and it is done, saith the Lord God. This is the day of which I have spoken. And the inhabitants of the cities of Israel shall go forth, and shall set on fire and burn the weapons, the shield, the spears and bows and arrows, and the handstaves and the pikes; and they shall burn them with fire seven years. And they shall not bring wood out of the countries, neither cut down out of the forests; for they shall burn the weapons with fire; and they shall spoil those that spoiled them, and rob those that robbed them, saith the Lord God. And it shall come to pass in that day, that I will give unto Gog a place there, a renowned sepulchre in Israel, the valley of them that pass by on the east of the sea; and it shall stop the noses of the passengers. And there shall they bury Gog and all his multitude, and they shall call it the valley of Hamon-gog. And the house of Israel shall be seven months burying them, that they may cleanse the land. Yea, all the people of the land shall bury them; and it shall be to them a renown, the day that I shall be glorified, saith the Lord God. And they shall appoint men continually who shall pass through the land to bury with the passengers those that remain upon the face of the earth, to cleanse it: after the end of seven months shall they search. And the passengers that pass through the land, when any seeth a man's bone, then shall he set up a sign by it, till the buriers have buried it in the valley of Hamon-gog. And also the name of the city shall be Hamonah; thus shall they cleanse the land. And thou, son of man, thus saith the Lord God: Speak unto every feathered fowl and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh and drink blood. Ye shall eat the flesh of the mighty, and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, of rams, of lambs, and of goats, of bullocks, all of them fatlings of Bashan. And ye shall eat fat till ye be full, and drink blood till ye be drunken, of my sacrifice which I have sacrificed for you. Thus ye shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with mighty men, and with all men of war, saith the Lord God. And I will set my glory among the nations, and all the nations shall see my judgment that I have executed, and my hand that I have laid upon them. So the house of Israel shall know that I am the Lord their God from that day and forward. And the nations shall know that the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity, because they trespassed against me, so that I hid my face from them, and gave them into the hand of their enemies; so they fell all of them by the sword. According to their uncleanness and their transgressions have I done unto them, and hid my face from them. Therefore thus saith the Lord God: Now will I bring again the captivity of Jacob, and have mercy upon the whole house of Israel, and will be jealous for my holy name. They shall bear their shame and all their trespasses which they have trespassed against me, when they shall dwell safely in their land, and none shall make them afraid; when I have brought them again from the peoples, and gathered them out of their enemies' lands, and am sanctified in them in the sight of many nations. Then shall they know that I am the Lord their God, because I caused them to be led into captivity among the nations, and have gathered them unto their own land, and have left none of them any more there. Neither will I hide my face any more from them, for I have poured out my spirit upon the whole house of Israel, saith the Lord God.

...twenty cubits. And having entered within he measured at the front of the gate two cubits, and the gate six cubits; and the width of the gate seven cubits. He measured also its length, twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits before the face of the temple. And he said to me: This is the Holy of Holies. And he measured the wall of the house, six cubits; and the width of the side chamber, four cubits, all around the house. The sides, side to side, were thirty-three (in some structure). There were projections which entered into the wall of the house around the sides, so that they might be contained and not touch the wall of the temple. And there was a passage going round upward by a winding stair, and it went up by circuit into the innermost part of the temple. Therefore the temple was wider in the upper parts, and so from the lower it ascended to the higher, and to the middle. And I saw in the house a height all around; the sides were founded according to the measure of a reed, six cubits' space; and the width through the outer wall of the side, five cubits. And the inner house was within the sides of the house. And between the treasure chambers the width was twenty cubits all around the house on every side. And there was a door of the side toward prayer: one door toward the north way, and one door toward the south way; and the width of the place for prayer, five cubits all around. And the building which was set apart, turned toward the way looking to the sea, was seventy cubits wide; but the wall of the building was five cubits wide all around, and its length ninety cubits. And he measured the house, its length a hundred cubits; and what was separate, the building and its walls, was a hundred cubits in length. And the width before the face of the house, and of that which was separated toward the east, a hundred cubits. And he measured the length...

...of the building facing that which was set apart at the back, with windows on either side, a hundred cubits; and the inner temple, and the vestibules of the court, thresholds, and slanted windows, windows all around on three sides opposite each threshold, and it was floored with wood all around. The floor reached up to the windows, and the closed windows were above the doors, and up to the inner house, and outside, over every wall all around, within and without, according to measure; and cherubim and palm trees were wrought, a palm between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces: the face of a man toward the palm on one side, and the face of a lion toward the palm on the other side, expressed thus throughout the whole house all around, from the ground up to the higher part. Cherubim and palm trees were represented on the wall of the temple. The threshold was square, and the appearance of the sanctuary was opposite the appearance [of the temple]. The wooden altar was three cubits high, and its length two cubits, and its corners, and its length, and its walls were of wood. And he spoke to me: This is the table before the Lord. And there were two doors in the temple and in the sanctuary, and in the two doors on either side there were double leaves, which folded upon themselves; for there were double doors on either side of the doorways. And there were carved on the doors of the temple cherubim and the sculpture of palm trees, just as they were represented on the walls. Wherefore also thicker were the beams at the front of the vestibule outside, above which were slanted windows, and the likeness of palm trees on this side and that on the shoulders of the vestibule, according to the sides of the house and the width of the walls. ...opposite the separate building, and beyond the same, facing north, in the length one hundred cubits of the north door, and fifty cubits wide, beyond twenty cubits of the inner court; and beyond the pavement laid with stone of the outer court, where there was a portico joined to a triple portico. And before the chambers there was a walk ten cubits wide, looking toward the interior, one cubit in width. And their doors were toward the north, where the chambers were lower in the upper parts, because the portico above supported them, standing out from the lower and middle buildings. For there were three storeys, and they did not have columns as the columns of the outer courts had. Therefore they stood out from the lower and middle levels, fifty cubits from the ground. And the outer enclosure, according to the chambers that were on the way of the outer court, before the chambers—its length was fifty cubits; for the length of the chambers of the outer court was fifty cubits, and the length before the face of the temple was a hundred cubits. And beneath these chambers was the entrance from the east for those entering into it from the outer court, in the width of the enclosure of the court which was opposite the east way, before the face of the separate building. And there were chambers before the building, and a way before their face, like the pattern of the chambers that were on the north way. According to their length, so also their width, and all their entrances, and their likenesses, and their doors, according to the doors of the chambers that faced south. There was a door at the head of the way, which was before the separate vestibule, for those entering by the east way. And he said to me: The chambers of the north and the chambers of the south, which are before the separate building — these are

the holy chambers, in which the priests who draw near to the Lord eat the most holy things. There they shall place the most holy things, and the offering for sin and for trespass, for the place is holy. And when the priests go out, they shall not go out from the holy places into the outer court; but there they shall lay up their garments in which they minister, for they are holy; and they shall put on other garments, and so approach to the people. And when he had finished the measurements of the inner house, he brought me out by the way of the gate that looked toward the east, and he measured it all around. He measured on the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around. And he measured on the north side five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around. And on the south side he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed all around. And on the west side he measured five hundred reeds by the measuring reed. On all four sides he measured it: the length five hundred cubits and the width five hundred cubits. And the wall divides between the sanctuary and the place of the common people.

And he brought me to the gate that looked toward the east way. [The priests] entered the inner court. And they shall not take as wives a widow or one divorced, but virgins of the seed of the house of Israel. But the widow who was the widow of a priest they may take. And they shall teach my people the difference between the holy and the profane, and cause them to discern between the unclean and the clean. And in a controversy they shall stand to judge according to my judgments; and they shall keep my laws and my precepts in all my solemnities, and they shall hallow my sabbaths. They shall not go in to a dead man, lest they be defiled, except for father, mother, son, daughter, brother, or sister who has had no husband — for these they may defile themselves. And after he is cleansed they shall reckon to him seven days, and on the day of his entering into the sanctuary, into the inner court, to minister to me in the sanctuary, he shall offer for his sin, says the Lord God. And they shall have no inheritance: I am their inheritance, and you shall give them no possession in Israel; for I am their possession. They shall eat the sacrifice for sin and for trespass; and every devoted thing in Israel shall be theirs. And the first of all the firstfruits and all the offerings of everything that is offered shall belong to the priests. You shall also give to the priest the first of your dough, that he may cause a blessing to rest on your house. The priests shall not eat anything that dies of itself, or is torn, whether of birds or of beasts. Chapter 45.

When you divide the land by lot, you shall set apart a portion for the Lord, a holy portion of the land, twenty-five thousand [reeds] in length, and ten thousand in breadth. This shall be holy in all its borders round about. And of this there shall be for the sanctuary five hundred by five hundred, foursquare, round about, and fifty cubits for the suburbs round about. And by this measure you shall measure the length of twenty-five thousand and the breadth of ten thousand.

And in it shall be the temple and the holy of holies: the sanctified portion of the land shall belong to the priests, the ministers of the sanctuary, who draw near to minister to the Lord. It shall be a place for their houses and a holy place for the sanctuary. Twenty-five thousand in length and ten thousand in breadth shall belong to the Levites who minister in the house; they shall possess twenty chambers. And of the possession of the city you shall give five thousand in breadth and twenty-five thousand in length, according to the portion of the sanctuary, for the whole house of Israel. And for the prince there shall be a portion on this side and on that side of the holy portion of the sanctuary and of the possession of the city, in front of the portion of the sanctuary and in front of the possession of the city, on the west side toward the sea, and on the east side toward the east; and the length shall be equal to one of the portions, from the west border to the east border. This shall be his possession in Israel. And the princes shall no more oppress my people, but they shall give the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes. Thus says the Lord God: Let it suffice you, O princes of Israel: remove violence and spoil, and execute judgment and justice, take away your exactions from my people, says the Lord God. You shall have just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath. The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, so that the bath may contain the tenth part of a homer, and the ephah the tenth part of a homer: the measure shall be according to the homer. And the shekel shall be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, and fifteen shekels shall make your maneh. And this is the offering which you shall offer: the sixth part of an ephah from a homer of wheat, and the sixth part of an ephah from a homer of barley. Concerning the ordinance of oil, the bath of oil: you shall offer the tenth part of a bath out of the homer, for ten baths make a homer. And one ram out of the flock, out of two hundred, from those that feed Israel, for a meat offering, and for a burnt offering, and for peace offerings, to make atonement for them, says the Lord God. All the people of the land shall be obliged to give this offering to the prince in Israel.

[marginal note] And ten baths make a homer.

"I confess and praise thee, that thou hast given me wisdom and strength, and now hast shown me what we asked of thee: for thou hast revealed to us the king's matter." After this Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon, and he spoke to him thus: "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation." Then Arioch hastily brought Daniel in before the king and said to him: "I have found a man among the sons of the captivity of Judah who will make known the interpretation to the king." The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar: "Are you truly able to show me the dream that I saw, and its interpretation?" And Daniel answered before the king and said: "The mystery that the king asks about, the wise men, magicians, enchanters, and soothsayers cannot show to the king; but there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, who has made known to you, King Nebuchadnezzar, what will come to pass in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed were these. You, O king, began to think in your bed what would happen hereafter; and he who reveals mysteries has shown you what is to come. As for me, not because of wisdom that is in me more than in all the living has this mystery been revealed, but that the interpretation might be made known to the king, and that you might know the thoughts of your mind. You, O king, were watching, and behold, as it were a great statue. That statue, great and of exceeding height, stood before you, and its appearance was terrible. This statue's head was of fine gold, its breast and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, its legs of iron, and its feet part iron and part clay. You watched until a stone was cut out without hands and struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and broke them in pieces. Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were broken together and became like chaff from a summer threshing floor, which the wind carried away, so that no place was found for them. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth. This is the dream, and we will tell its interpretation before you, O king. You are king of kings; the God of heaven has given you kingdom, power, might, and glory, and has given into your hand all in which the sons of men dwell, and the beasts of the field, and the birds of the sky, and has made you ruler over them all. You are, therefore, the head of gold. And after you shall arise another kingdom, inferior to yours, of silver, and a third kingdom of bronze, which shall rule over the whole earth. And a fourth kingdom shall be like iron; as iron breaks and subdues all things, so this kingdom shall break and crush all these. Furthermore, as you saw the feet and toes partly of potter's clay and partly of iron, the kingdom shall be divided, yet there shall be in it something of the strength of iron, since you saw iron mixed with miry clay. And the toes of the feet being partly iron and partly clay, the kingdom shall be partly strong and partly broken. And as you saw iron mixed with miry clay, they shall mingle with the seed of men, but they shall not adhere to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay. And in the days of those kingdoms the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, and this kingdom shall not be left to another people; it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand forever. Since you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain without hands, and that it broke in pieces the clay, the iron, the bronze, the silver, and the gold, the great God has made known to the king what shall come to pass hereafter; and the dream is true, and its interpretation is faithful." Hear the word of the Lord, O children of Israel: for the Lord has a judgment with the inhabitants of the land. For there is no truth, and there is no mercy, and there is no knowledge of God in the land. Cursing, and lying, and killing, and theft, and adultery have overflowed, and blood has touched blood. Because of this the land shall mourn, and everyone who dwells in it shall languish, with the beasts of the field, and the birds of the air; yea, the fish of the sea also shall be gathered together. Yet let no man contend, and let no man be rebuked: for your people are as those who contradict the priest. Therefore you shall fall today, and the prophet also shall fall with you: I have made your mother be silent in the night. My people are silenced, because they have no knowledge: because you have rejected knowledge, I will reject you, that you shall not serve me as priest. You have forgotten the law of your God: I also will forget your children. According to the multitude of them, so they have sinned against me: I will change their glory into shame. They eat the sins of my people, and lift up their souls to their iniquity. And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest. I will visit upon him his ways, and I will repay him his devices. And they shall eat, and shall not be satisfied: they have committed fornication, and have not ceased: because they have left off to take heed to the Lord. Fornication and wine and drunkenness take away the heart. My people ask counsel at their stocks, and their staff declares to them: for the spirit of fornication has deceived them, and they have gone astray from their God. They sacrifice upon the tops of the mountains, and burn incense upon the hills, under oaks and poplars and elms, because the shadow of it is good. Therefore your daughters shall commit fornication, and your spouses shall be adulteresses. I will not visit upon your daughters when they commit fornication, nor upon your spouses when they commit adultery: because...

they themselves conversed with harlots, and sacrificed with the effeminate: and the people who do not understand shall be beaten. If you play the harlot, O Israel, let not Judah offend at least. And do not enter into Gilgal, and do not go up to Bethaven, and do not swear, 'The Lord lives': For as a heifer wanton and unruly has Israel gone astray. Now the Lord shall feed them as a lamb in a large place. Ephraim is joined to idols: let him alone. Their banquet is separated: they have committed fornication continually: her rulers have loved to bring shame. The wind has bound her up in its wings, and they shall be ashamed because of their sacrifices. Chapter 5.

Hear this, O priests, and hearken, O house of Israel, and give ear, O house of the king: for judgment is toward you, because you have been a snare on Mizpah, and a net spread upon Tabor. And the victims you have made deep [in slaughter]. But I am the instructor of them all. I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me: for now Ephraim has committed fornication, Israel is defiled. They will not set their thoughts to return to their God: for the spirit of fornication is in the midst of them, and they have not known the Lord. And the pride of Israel shall testify to his face: and Israel and Ephraim shall fall in their iniquity; Judah also shall fall with them. With their flocks and with their herds they shall go to seek the Lord, and shall not find him: he has withdrawn himself from them. They have dealt treacherously against the Lord: for they have begotten strange children. Now the new moon shall devour them along with their portions. Blow the trumpet in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah: cry aloud at Bethaven, behind you, O Benjamin. Ephraim shall be desolate in the day of rebuke: among the tribes of Israel I have made known what is sure. results.translation: The faces of all are like the blackness of a pot. Where is the dwelling of the lions, and the pasture of the lions' whelps? To which the lion went, that he might enter there, the lion's whelp, and there was none to make him afraid. The lion caught sufficiently for his whelps, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his caves with prey, and his den with ravin. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword shall devour thy young lions: and I will cut off thy prey from the earth, and the voice of thy messengers shall no more be heard. Chapter III. Woe to the bloody city, all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not. The noise of a whip, and the noise of the rattling of the wheels, and of the pransing horses, and of the jumping chariots. The horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering spear: and there is a multitude of slain, and a great number of carcasses; and there is no end of their corpses; they stumble upon their corpses: because of the multitude of the whoredoms of the well-favored harlot, the mistress of witchcrafts, that selleth nations through her whoredoms, and families through her witchcrafts. Behold, I am against thee, saith the Lord of hosts; and I will discover thy skirts upon thy face, and I will shew the nations thy nakedness, and the kingdoms thy shame. And I will cast abominable filth upon thee, and make thee vile, and will set thee as a gazingstock. And it shall come to pass, that all they that look upon thee shall flee from thee, and say, Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her? Whence shall I seek comforters for thee? Art thou better than populous Alexandria, that was situate among the rivers, that had the waters round about it, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea? Ethiopia and Egypt were her strength, and it was infinite; Put and Lubim were thy helpers. Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity: her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets: and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains. Thou also shalt be drunken: thou shalt be hid, thou also shalt seek a refuge from the enemy. All thy strongholds shall be like fig trees with the firstripe figs: if they be shaken, they shall even fall into the mouth of the eater. Behold, thy people in the midst of thee are women: the gates of thy land shall be set wide open unto thine enemies: the fire shall devour thy bars. Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strongholds: go into clay, and tread the mortar, make strong the brick kiln. There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off, it shall eat thee up like the cankerworm: make thyself many as the cankerworm, make thyself many as the locusts. Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven: the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away. Thy crowned are as the locusts, and thy captains as the great grasshoppers, which camp in the hedges in the cold day, but when the sun ariseth they flee away, and their place is not known where they are. Thy shepherds slumber, O king of Assyria: thy nobles shall dwell in the dust: thy people is scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathereth them. There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous: all that hear the report of thee shall clap their hands over thee: for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually? Here ends the prophecy of Nahum. Here begins the prophecy of Habakkuk, chapter 1. The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see. O Lord, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! even cry out unto thee of violence, and thou wilt not save! Why dost thou shew me iniquity, and cause me to behold grievance? for spoiling and violence are before me: and there is strife, and contention riseth up. Therefore the law is slacked, and judgment doth never go forth: for the wicked doth compass about the righteous...

dices. Si tulerit homo carnem sanctifi-catam in ora vestimenti sui et tetigerit de summitate eius panem aut pulmentum aut vinum aut oleum aut omnem cibum: nunquid sanctificabit? Respondentes autem sacerdotes dixerunt. Non. Et dixit aggeus. Si tetigerit pollutus in anima ex omnibus his nunquid contaminabitur? Et responderunt sacerdotes: et dixerunt. Contaminabitur. Et respondit aggeus et dixit. Sic populus iste et sic gens ista ante faciem meam dicit dominus: et sic omne opus manuum eorum: et omnia que obtulerunt ibi contaminata erunt. Et nunc ponite corda vestra a die hac et supra antequam ponetur lapis super lapidem in templo domini: cum accederetis ad acervum viginti modiorum et fierent decem: et intraretis ad torcular ut exprimeretis quinquaginta lagenas et fiebant viginti. Percussi vos vento urente: et aurugine et grandine omnia opera manuum vestrarum: et non fuit in vobis qui reverteretur ad me dicit dominus. Ponite corda vestra ex die ista et in futurum a die vicesima et quarta noni mensis: a die qua fundamenta iacta sunt templi domini ponite super cor vestrum. Nunquid iam semen in germine est? Et adhuc vinea et ficus et malogranatum et lignum olive non floruit. Ex die ista benedicam. Et factum est verbum domini secundo ad aggeum in vicesima et quarta mensis dicens. Loquere ad zorobabel ducem iude dicens. Ego movebo celum pariter et terram: et subvertam solium regnorum: et conteram fortitudinem regni gentium. Et subvertam quadrigam et ascensorem eius: et descendent equi et ascensores eorum: vir in gladio fratris sui. In die illo dicit dominus exercituum assumam te

zorobabel fili salatiel serve meus dicit dominus: et ponam te quasi signaculum: quia te elegi dicit dominus exercituum. Explicit aggeus prophetia. Incipit zachariae prophetia. Capitulum I.

In mense octavo in anno secundo darii regis: factum est verbum domini ad zachariam filium barachie filii addo prophetam. Iratus est dominus super patres vestros iracundia. Et dices ad eos. Hec dicit dominus exercituum. Convertimini ad me ait dominus exercituum: et convertar ad vos dicit dominus exercituum. Ne sitis sicut patres vestri ad quos clamabant prophete priores dicentes hec dicit dominus exercituum: convertimini de viis vestris malis et cogitationibus vestris pessimis: et non audierunt neque attenderunt ad me dicit dominus. Patres vestri ubi sunt et prophete? Numquid in sempiternum vivent? Verumtamen verba mea et legitima mea que mandavi servis meis prophetis: nunquid non comprehenderunt patres vestros? Et conversi sunt et dixerunt. Sicut cogitavit dominus exercituum facere nobis secundum vias nostras et secundum adinventiones nostras: fecit nobis. In die vicesima et quarta undecimi mensis sabbath in anno secundo darii: factum est verbum domini ad zachariam filium barachie filii addo prophetam dicens. Vidi per noctem: et ecce vir ascendens super equum rufum: et ipse stabat inter myrtera que erant in profundo: et post eum equi rufi varii et albi. Et dixi. Qui sunt isti domine mi? Et dixit ad me angelus domini qui loquebatur in me. Ego ostendam tibi quid sunt hec. Et respondit vir qui stabat inter myrtera et dixit. Isti sunt quos misit dominus: ut perambulent terram. Et responderunt angelo domini qui stabat inter myrtera: et dixerunt. Peragravimus terram: et ecce omnis terra habitatur et quiescit. Et respondit

[Aggeus/Haggai continues]: ...says (the Lord). If a man carries sanctified flesh in the fold of his garment, and touches with the fold bread, or pottage, or wine, or oil, or any food, shall it be sanctified? And the priests answered and said: No. And Aggeus said: If one that is unclean by reason of touching the body of one who died touches any of these, shall it be defiled? And the priests answered and said: It shall be defiled. And Aggeus answered and said: So is this people, and so is this nation before my face, says the Lord, and so is every work of their hands: and all that they have offered there shall be defiled. And now consider from this day forward, before a stone was laid upon a stone in the temple of the Lord: when you came to a heap of twenty measures, there were but ten: when you came to the press, to press out fifty vessels, there were but twenty. I struck you with a burning wind, and with blight, and with hail all the works of your hands: and there was none among you that returned to me, says the Lord. Set your hearts, from this day and forward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day on which the foundations of the temple of the Lord were laid: consider it in your heart. Is the seed yet in bud? Or does the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree, which have not yet budded, remain so? From this day I will bless. And the word of the Lord came a second time to Aggeus, in the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying: Speak to Zorobabel, ruler of Judah, saying: I will move heaven and earth together: and I will overturn the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the strength of the kingdom of the Gentiles: and I will overthrow the chariot and him that rides in it: and the horses and their riders shall come down, every one by the sword of his brother. In that day, says the Lord of hosts, I will take you, Zorobabel, son of Salathiel, my servant, says the Lord, and will make you as a signet, for I have chosen you, says the Lord of hosts.

Here ends the prophecy of Aggeus. Here begins the prophecy of Zacharias. Chapter I.

In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius the king, the word of the Lord came to Zacharias the son of Barachias, son of Addo, the prophet, saying: The Lord has been exceedingly angry with your fathers. And you shall say to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn to me, says the Lord of hosts, and I will turn to you, says the Lord of hosts. Be not as your fathers, to whom the former prophets cried, saying: Thus says the Lord of hosts: Turn from your evil ways, and from your wicked thoughts: but they did not hear, nor listen to me, says the Lord. Where are your fathers, and the prophets? Do they live forever? Yet my words and my statutes, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your fathers? And they turned and said: As the Lord of hosts thought to do to us, according to our ways and according to our devices, so has he done to us. On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is Sabbath, in the second year of Darius, the word of the Lord came to Zacharias the son of Barachias, son of Addo, the prophet, saying: I saw in the night, and behold a man riding upon a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees, which were in the bottom: and behind him were red, speckled, and white horses. And I said: Who are these, my lord? And the angel of the Lord who spoke in me said to me: I will show you what these are. And the man who stood among the myrtle trees answered and said: These are they whom the Lord has sent to walk through the earth. And they answered the angel of the Lord who stood among the myrtle trees, and said: We have walked through the earth: and behold, all the earth is inhabited, and is at rest. And he answered...

...in the mountains: and he himself came out against them. But those lying in ambush arose from their places and joined battle. And all who were on Jonathan's side fled, and none was left of them except Mattathias son of Absalom and Judas son of Chalphi, the commander of the army. And Jonathan tore his garments and put earth on his head and prayed. Then Jonathan returned to them in battle and turned them to flight and they fought. And when those who had fled from his side saw it, they returned to him, and all pursued together with him even to Kedesh, to their camp, and came thither. And there fell of the foreigners on that day three thousand men, and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem. Chapter 12.

And Jonathan saw that the time favored him, and he chose men and sent them to Rome to establish and renew friendship with them. And to the Spartans and to other places he sent letters after the same form. And they went to Rome and entered the senate house and said: Jonathan the high priest and the nation of the Jews sent us to renew friendship and alliance according to the former terms. And they gave them letters to the places, that they might conduct them into the land of Judah in peace. And this is the copy of the letters which Jonathan wrote to the Spartans: Jonathan the high priest, and the elders of the nation, and the priests, and the rest of the people of the Jews, to their brethren the Spartans, greeting. Already before this letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Darius who reigned among you, that you are our brethren, as the writing subjoined shows. having as consolation the holy books which are in our hands, preferred to send to you to renew brotherhood and friendship, lest we should become strangers to you. We therefore at all times without ceasing, on feast days and other proper occasions, remember you in the sacrifices we offer and in our observances, as it is right and fitting to remember brethren. We rejoice, moreover, in your glory. But as for us, many tribulations and many wars have encompassed us, and the kings round about us have fought against us. We were unwilling therefore to be troublesome to you, nor to our other allies and friends in these wars. For we had help from heaven, and we were delivered, and our enemies were humbled. We therefore chose Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason, and sent them to the Romans to renew with them the friendship and former alliance. Matthew.

...it were better for him that a millstone should be hung about his neck, and that he should be drowned in the depth of the sea. Woe to the world because of scandals! For it must needs be that scandals come, but woe to that man by whom the scandal comes. And if thy hand or thy foot scandalize thee, cut it off and cast it from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed or lame, than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire. And if thy eye scandalize thee, pluck it out and cast it from thee: it is better for thee having one eye to enter into life, than having two eyes to be cast into hell fire. See that you despise not one of these little ones: for I say to you that their angels in heaven always see the face of my Father who is in heaven. For the Son of man came to save that which was lost. What think you? If a man have a hundred sheep, and one of them should go astray, does he not leave the ninety-nine in the mountains, and go to seek that which is gone astray? And if it so be that he find it: Amen I say to you, he rejoices more for that than for the ninety-nine that went not astray. Even so it is not the will of your Father who is in heaven, that one of these little ones should perish. But if thy brother shall offend against thee, go and rebuke him between thee and him alone. If he shall hear thee, thou shalt gain thy brother. But if he will not hear thee, take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may stand. And if he will not hear them, tell the church. And if he will not hear the church, let him be to thee as the heathen and publican. Amen I say to you, whatsoever you shall bind upon earth shall be bound also in heaven, and whatsoever you shall loose upon earth shall be loosed also in heaven. Again I say to you, that if two of you shall consent upon earth concerning anything whatsoever they shall ask, it shall be done for them by my Father who is in heaven. For where there are two or three gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them. Then came Peter to him and said: Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Till seven times? Jesus said to him: I say not to thee till seven times, but till seventy times seven times. Therefore the kingdom of heaven is likened to a king who would take an account of his servants. And when he had begun to settle accounts, one was brought to him who owed him ten thousand talents. And as he had nothing to pay, his lord commanded that he be sold, and his wife and children, and all that he had, and payment be made. But that servant falling down besought him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. And the lord of that servant being moved with pity, let him go and forgave him the debt. But when that servant was gone out, he found one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred pence: and laying hold of him, he throttled him, saying: Pay what thou owest. And his fellow servant falling down, besought him, saying: Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. And he would not, but went and cast him into prison till he paid the debt. Now his fellow servants seeing what was done, were very sorry, and they came and told their lord all that was done. Then his lord called him, and said to him: Wicked servant, I forgave thee all the debt because thou besoughtest me: shouldst not thou then have had compassion also on thy fellow servant, even as I had compassion on thee? And his lord being angry, delivered him to the torturers, until he paid all the debt. So also shall my heavenly Father do to you, if you forgive not everyone his brother from your hearts. Chapter 19.

Potestis bibere calicem que ego bibo: aut baptismo quo ego baptizor baptizari? At illi dixerunt ei. Possum9. Ihesus autem ait eis. Calicem quide que ego bibo bibetis 7 baptismu quo ego baptizor baptizabimini: sedere aut ad dexteram mea uel ad sinistra non est meum dare uobis: sed quibus paratu est. Et audientes dece indignari sunt de iacobo et iohanne. Ihesus autem uocans eos ait illis. Scitis qa hij qui uidentur principari gentibus dominant eis: et principes eor potestatem habent ipsor. Non ita est autem in uobis: sed quicuqz voluerit fieri maior erit vester minister: et quicuqz voluerit in vobis primus esse: erit omniu seruus. Nam et filius hois non venit ut ministraretur ei. sed ut ministraret: et daret animam suam redemptionem pro multis. Et veniunt ihericho. Et proficiscente eo de ihericho·et discipulis ei9 7 plurima multitudine: filius thimei bartimeus cecus·sedebat iuxta viam mendicans. Qui cum audisset quia ihesus nazarenus est: cepit clamare 7 dicere. Ihesu fili david: miserere mei. Et cominabantur illi multi·ut taceret. At ille multo magis clamabat: fili david miserere mei. Et stas ihesus: precepit illu vocari. Et vocant cecum:dicentes ei. Animequior esto. Surge:vocat te. Qui proiecto vestimento suo·exiliens venit ad eu. Et respondens ihesus dixit illi. Quid tibi vis faciam? Cecus autem dixit ei. Rabboni ut videam. Ihesus autem ait illi. V ade. Fides tua te salvum fecit. Et cofestim vidit:et sequebatur eum in via. c.xi.

[E]t cum appropinquarent ihierosolime et bethanie ad montem oliuarum mittit duos ex discipulis suis:et ait illis. Ite in castellum qd contra vos est: et statim introeuntes illuc·invenietis pullum ligatum·super que nemo adhuc hominum sedit. Soluite illum:et adducite. Et si quis vobis dixerit quid facitis:dicite quia domino necessari9 est: et continuo illu dimittet huc. Et abeuntes invenerut pullum ligatum·ante ianuam foris in biuio:7 soluerunt eum. Et quidam de illic stantibus dicebant illis. Quid facitis solventes pullum? Qui dixerunt eis sicut preceperat illis ihesus:et dimiserunt eis. Et duxerunt pullum ad ihesum:et imponunt illi vestimenta sua et sedit super eum. Multi vesti menta sua strauerunt in via. Alij autem frondes cedebant de arboribus: et sternebant in via. Et qui precedebant·et qui sequebantur clamabant dicentes. Osanna benedictus qui venit in nomine dni:benedictum qd venit regnu patris nostri david: osanna in excelsis. Et introivit ihierosolimam in templum: et circumspectis omnibus cu iam vespera esset hora:exiit in bethaniam cum duodeci. Et alia die cum exiret a bethania esurijt. What is right, do you not judge for yourselves? When you go with your adversary to the ruler, on the way take pains to be delivered from him, lest he drag you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and the officer cast you into prison. I say to you: you shall not get out from there until you have paid even the last penny.

There were present at that very time some who told him of the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices. And Jesus answering said to them: Do you suppose that these Galileans were sinners above all the Galileans because they suffered such things? I tell you, no; but unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish. Or those eighteen upon whom the tower in Siloam fell and killed them: do you suppose that they were debtors above all men dwelling in Jerusalem? I tell you, no; but unless you repent, you shall all likewise perish.

He also spoke this parable: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he came seeking fruit on it and found none. Then he said to the keeper of the vineyard: Behold, for three years I have come seeking fruit on this fig tree and find none. Cut it down; why does it also use up the ground? But he answering said to him: Lord, let it alone this year also, until I dig around it and put manure. And if it bears fruit, well; but if not, then after that you shall cut it down.

And he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath. And behold, a woman who had a spirit of infirmity for eighteen years, and was bent over and could in no way lift herself up. Whom when Jesus saw, he called her to him and said to her: Woman, you are freed from your infirmity. And he laid his hands on her, and immediately she was made straight, and glorified God.

And the ruler of the synagogue, answering, being indignant because Jesus had healed on the sabbath, said to the crowd: There are six days in which men ought to work; in them therefore come and be healed, and not on the sabbath day. The Lord then answering him said: Hypocrites, does not each of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the manger and lead it away to water it? And ought not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound, behold, these eighteen years, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day? And when he said these things, all his adversaries were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced at all the glorious things that were done by him.

He said therefore: To what is the kingdom of God like, and to what shall I compare it? It is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and cast into his garden, and it grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the air lodged in its branches. And again he said: To what shall I compare the kingdom of God? It is like leaven which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole was leavened.

And he went through the cities and towns teaching, and journeying toward Jerusalem. Then someone said to him: Lord, are there few that be saved? And he said to them: Strive to enter in at the narrow gate, for many, I say to you, will seek to enter and shall not be able. When once the master of the house has risen up and shut the door, and you begin to stand outside and knock at the door, saying: Lord, open to us; and he will answer and say to you: I know you not, where you are from. Then you will begin to say: We have eaten and drunk in your presence, and you have taught in our streets. And he will say: I tell you, I know you not, where you are from; depart from me, all you workers of iniquity. There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when you shall see Abraham and Isaac and Jacob and all

et in retributione illis. Obscurentur oculi eorũ ne videãt: 3 dorsũ eox semp incurua. Dico ergo. Nũqd sic offenderũt ut caderent? Absit. Sed illorũ delicto salus gentibus: ut illos emulem̃. Nõ si delictum eorũ diuitie sunt mũdi: 3 diminuto eox diuitie gentiũ: quatomagis plenitudo eorũ? Uobis eni dico gentibz. Quãdiu quidẽ ego sum gentiũ apstus ministeriũ meũ hõnorificabo: si quo modo ad emulandum puocem carnẽ meã: 3 saluos faciam aliquos ex illis. Si eni amissio eorũ reconciliatio ẽ mũdi: q̃ assumptio nisi vita ex mortuis? Nõ si delibatio sancta est: 3 massa. Et si radix sancta: et rami. Nõ si aliqui ex ramis fracti sunt: tu aũt cũ oleaster esses insertus es in illis: 3 socius radicis 3 pinguedinis oliue factus es: noli gloriari aduersu ramos. Nõ si gloriaris: nõ tu radicem portas: sed radix te. Dicis ergo. Fracti sunt rami: ut ego insterar. Bene. Propter incredulitatem fracti sũt. Tu aũt fide stas. Noli altũ sapere sed time. Si eni deus naturalibz ramis nõ pepercit: ne forte nec tibi parcat. Vide ergo bonitatem 3 seueritatẽ dei. In eos quidẽ qui ceciderũt seueritatem: in te aũt bonitatem dei: si pmanseris i bonitate. Alioquin 3 tu excideris. Sed 3 illi si nõ pmãserint i incredulitate inserentur. Potens est enim de9 iterũ inserere illos. Nã 3 si tu ex naturali excisus es oleastro 3 contra naturã insertus es in bonã oliuã: quãtomagis hij qui secundũ naturã inserentur sue oliue? Nolo eni vos ignorare fres misteriũ hoc: ut nõ sitis vobisipis sapientes: quia cecitas ex parte contingit in isrl' donec plenitudo gentiũ intraret: 3 sic omis israhel saluus fieret sicut scriptũ

est. Veniet ex syon: qui eripiat et auertat impietatem ab iacob. Et hoc illis a me testamentũ: cũ abstulero peccata eox. Secundũ euangeliũ quidẽ inimici pter vos: secundũ electionẽ aũt carissimi pter patres. Sine penitentia enim sunt dona 3 vocatio dei. Sicut enim aliquãdo et vos nõ credidistis deo nũc aũt misericordiã ᵃsecuti estis propter incredulitatẽ illorũ: ita et isti nũc nõ crediderũt i vestrã misericordiã: ut 3 ipi misericordiã cõsequãtur. Conclusit enim de9 omia in incredulitate: ut omniũ misereatur. O altitudo diuitiaz sapientie 3 scientie dei: quã incõprehensibilia sunt iudicia eius: et inuestigabiles vie ei9. Quis eni cognouit sensum dñi: aut quis cõsiliarius eius fuit? Aut quis prior dedit illi: et retribuetur ei? Quoniam ex ipso et per ipsum et in ipso sunt omnia: ipi gloria in secula seculorum amen. r.xii.

Obsecro itaq3 vos fratres per misericordiã dei: ut exhibeatis corpora vestra hostiã viuentem: sanctã deo placentem: rationabile obsequiũ vrm. Et nolite conformari huic seculo: sed reformamini in nouitate sensus vri: ut pbetis que sit volũtas dei bona 3 bene placens 3 pfecta. Dico enim per gratiã que data est michi: omibus q sunt inter vos: nõ plus sapere quã oportet sapere: sed sapere ad sobrietatem: 3 unicuiq3 sicut de9 diuisit mensurã fidei. Sicut eni in uno corpore multa membra habemus: omnia aũt membra nõ eundem actũ habent: ita multi unũ corpus sumus in xristo: singuli aũt alter alteri9 mẽbra: habentes donationes scdm gratiã que data est nobis differentes. Siue phetiam: scdm rationẽ fidei. Siue ministeriũ: i ministrando.

...and let it be to them for a recompense. Let their eyes be darkened that they may not see, and bow down their back always. I say then, Have they stumbled that they should fall? God forbid. But through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, to provoke them to jealousy. Now if the fall of them be the riches of the world, and the diminishing of them the riches of the Gentiles, how much more their fullness? For I speak to you Gentiles. Inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I magnify my office: if by any means I may provoke to emulation them which are my flesh, and might save some of them. For if the casting away of them be the reconciling of the world, what shall the receiving of them be, but life from the dead? For if the firstfruit be holy, the lump is also holy: and if the root be holy, so are the branches. And if some of the branches be broken off, and thou, being a wild olive tree, wert graffed in among them, and with them partakest of the root and fatness of the olive tree; boast not against the branches. But if thou boast, thou bearest not the root, but the root thee. Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be graffed in. Well; because of unbelief they were broken off, and thou standest by faith. Be not highminded, but fear: For if God spared not the natural branches, take heed lest he also spare not thee. Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be graffed in: for God is able to graff them in again. For if thou wert cut out of the olive tree which is wild by nature, and wert graffed contrary to nature into a good olive tree: how much more shall these, which be the natural branches, be graffed into their own olive tree? For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles be come in. And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written,

There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins. As concerning the gospel, they are enemies for your sakes: but as touching the election, they are beloved for the fathers' sakes. For the gifts and calling of God are without repentance. For as ye in times past have not believed God, yet have now obtained mercy through their unbelief: even so have these also now not believed, that through your mercy they also may obtain mercy. For God hath concluded them all in unbelief, that he might have mercy upon all. O the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! how unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways past finding out! For who hath known the mind of the Lord? or who hath been his counsellor? Or who hath first given to him, and it shall be recompensed unto him again? For of him, and through him, and to him, are all things: to whom be glory for ever. Amen. [Chapter 12]

I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service. And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God. For I say, through the grace given unto me, to every man that is among you, not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith. For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another. Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith; Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering.

For we are made partakers of Christ, if only we hold firm the beginning of his substance to the end; while it is said, Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts as in that provocation. For some who heard did provoke; but not all who went out of Egypt by Moses. And with whom was he angry forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bodies fell in the desert? And to whom did he swear that they should not enter into his rest, but to those who were unbelieving? So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.

Let us fear therefore, lest a promise being left of entering into his rest, any of you should seem to be wanting. For unto us was the gospel preached as well as unto them; but the word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in those who heard it. For we who have believed do enter into that rest, as he said, As I have sworn in my wrath, they shall not enter into my rest. And this, though the works were finished from the foundation of the world, for he spoke in a certain place of the seventh day thus: And God rested the seventh day from all his works. And in this place again, If they shall enter into my rest. Seeing then it remains that some must enter therein, and they to whom it was first preached entered not in because of unbelief, again he limits a certain day, saying in David, Today, after so long a time, as it is said, Today if you will hear his voice, harden not your hearts. For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not afterward have spoken of another day. There remains therefore a rest for the people of God. For he who has entered into his rest has also ceased from his own works, as God did from his.

Let us labor therefore to enter into that rest, lest anyone fall after the same example of unbelief. For the word of God is living and effectual, and more piercing than any two-edged sword, reaching even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of joints also and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. Neither is there any creature invisible in his sight: but all things are naked and open to the eyes of him to whom we must give account.

Seeing then that we have a great high priest who has passed into the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast our confession. For we have not a high priest who cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but was tempted in all things as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find grace to help in time of need.

For every high priest taken from among men is ordained for men in things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins: who can have compassion on the ignorant and on those who are out of the way, for he himself also is compassed with infirmity, and by reason thereof he ought, as for the people, so also for himself, to offer for sins. And no man takes this honor to himself, but he who is called of God, as was Aaron. So also Christ did not glorify himself to become a high priest, but he who said unto him, You are my Son, today have I begotten you. As also he says in another place, You are a priest forever after the order of Melchisedech. Who in the days of his flesh, when he had offered up prayers and supplications with strong crying and tears unto him who was able to save him from death, and was heard for his reverence; though he was a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered; and being made perfect...

"the testament which I will dispose to the house of Israel after those days," says the Lord, "giving my laws into their mind and writing them upon their hearts: and I will be to them a God, and they shall be to me a people. And no man shall teach his neighbor, and no man his brother, saying, Know the Lord: for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest: for I will be merciful to their unrighteousness, and their sins I will remember no more." In saying a new one, he made the former old. And that which decays and grows old is near vanishing away. Chapter 9.

The first covenant indeed had ordinances of divine service, and a worldly sanctuary. For a tabernacle was made; the first, in which was the candlestick, and the table, and the setting forth of the loaves, which is called the Sanctuary. And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holy of Holies, having a golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, in which was a golden urn holding manna, and Aaron's rod that had budded, and the tables of the covenant; and over it the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat; of which we cannot now speak in detail. Now these things being thus ordained, the priests always went into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of sacrifices. But into the second, only the high priest went once a year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the errors of the people: the Holy Spirit signifying by this that the way into the holy places was not yet made manifest, while the first tabernacle was still standing. Arise therefore and go down, and go with them, doubting nothing, for I have sent them. Then Peter went down to the men and said: Behold, I am he whom you seek. What is the reason why you have come? They said: Cornelius the centurion, a just man and one who fears God, and having a good report from the whole nation of the Jews, was warned by a holy angel to send for you into his house, and to hear words from you. The next day he entered Caesarea: and Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his relatives and close friends. And it happened that when Peter entered, Cornelius met him, and falling down at his feet, worshiped him. But Peter lifted him up, saying: Stand up; I myself am also a man. And talking with him he went in, and found many who had come together, and said to them: You know how unlawful it is for a Jewish man to join himself or come near to one of another nation. But God has shown me that I should not call any man common or unclean. Therefore I came without objection, having been sent for. I ask therefore for what reason you have sent for me.
