Actus.

Salamina: predicabat verbum dei in synagogis iudeorum. Habebant autem et iohannem in ministerio. Et cum perambulassent uniuersam insulam usque paphum: invenerunt quendam virum magum pseudoprophetam iudeum cui nomen erat bariesu: qui erat cum proconsule sergio paulo viro prudente. Hic accersitis barnaba et paulo: desiderabat audire verbum dei. Resistebat autem illis elymas magus: sic enim interpretatur nomen eius: querens auertere proconsulem a fide. Paulus autem qui et paulus: repletus spiritu sancto intuens in eum dixit. O plene omni dolo et omni fallacia fili diaboli-inimice omnis iustitie: non desinis subuertere vias domini rectas? Et nunc ecce manus domini super te: et eris cecus non videns solem usque ad tempus. Et confestim cecidit in eum caligo et tenebre: et circuiens querebat qui ei manum daret. Tunc proconsul cum vidisset factum credidit: ammirans super doctrina domini.
Et cum a papho nauigassent paulus et qui cum eo erant: venerunt pergen pamphilie. Iohannes autem discedens ab eis: reuersus est ierosolimam. Illi vero pertranseuntes pergen venerunt antiochiam pisidie: et ingressi synagogam die sabbatorum sederunt. Post lectionem autem legis et prophetarum: miserunt principes synagoge ad eos dicentes. Viri fratres: si quis est in vobis sermo exhortationis ad plebem dicite. Surgens autem paulus: et manu silentium indicens ait. Viri israhelite et qui timetis deum audite. Deus plebis israel elegit patres nostros et plebem exaltauit cum essent incole in terra egipti: et in brachio excelso eduxit eos ex ea: et per quadraginta annos tempus mores eorum sustinuit in deserto. Et destruens gentes septem in terra chanaan sorte distribuit eis terram eorum quasi post quadrigentos

et quinquaginta annos: et post hec dedit iudices usque ad samuel prophetam. Et exinde postulauerunt regem: et dedit illis saul filium cis-virum de tribu beniamin-annis quadraginta. Et amoto illo suscitauit illis dauid regem: cui testimonium philens dixit. Inueni dauid filium iesse virum secundum cor meum: qui faciet omnes voluntates meas. Huius deus ex semine secundum promissionem eduxit israel saluatorem ihesum: predicante iohanne ante faciem aduentus eius baptismum penitentie omni populo israel. Cum impleret autem cursum suum dicebat. Quem me arbitramini esse non sum ego: sed ecce venit post me: cuius non sum dignus calciamenta pedum soluere. Viri fratres-filij generis abraham et qui in vobis timent deum: vobis verbum salutis huius missum est. Qui enim habitabant ihrusalem et principes eius huc ignorantes et voces prophetarum que per omnia sabbata leguntur: iudicantes impleuerunt. Et nullam causam mortis inuenientes in eo: petierunt a pilato ut interficerent eum. Cumque consummassent omnia que de eo scripta erant: deponentes eum de ligno posuerunt eum in monumento.
Deus autem suscitauit eum a mortuis tercia die: qui visus est per dies multos hiis qui simul ascenderant cum eo de galilea in ierusalem: qui usque nunc sunt testes eius ad plebem. Et nos vobis annuntiamus eam quae ad patres nostros repromissio facta est: quia hanc deus adimpleuit filijs vestris resuscitans ihesum sicut et in psalmo secundo scriptum est. Filius meus es tu: ego hodie genui te. Quod autem suscitauit eum a mortuis amplius iam non reuersurum in corruptionem: ita dixit. Quia dabo vobis sancta dauid fidelia. Ideoque et alias dicit. …they were. After three months we sailed in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered in the island, whose sign was the Twins (Castor and Pollux). And when we came to Syracuse we stayed there three days. From there, sailing around, we came to Rhegium, and after one day the south wind blew, and on the second day we came to Puteoli, where we found brethren who asked us to stay with them seven days; and so we came to Rome. And when the brothers there heard of us, they came out to meet us as far as Appii Forum and the Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, giving thanks to God, he took courage. And when we had come to Rome, Paul was allowed to stay by himself with a soldier who guarded him. After the third day he called together the leaders of the Jews. And when they had come together he said to them, "Men and brethren, I have done nothing against the law or the customs of our fathers; yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans, who, when they had examined me, wished to release me, because there was no cause of death in me. But when the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar—not as having anything to accuse my own nation of. For this cause therefore I asked to see you and speak with you; for it is because of the hope of Israel that I am bound with this chain." And they said to him, "We have neither received letters concerning you from Judea, nor has any of the brethren who came reported or spoken anything evil of you. But we desire to hear from you what you think, for concerning this sect we know that it is spoken against everywhere." And when they had appointed him a day, many came to him at his lodging; to whom he expounded, testifying the kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the Law of Moses and from the prophets, from morning until evening. And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not. And when they were not in agreement among themselves, they departed, Paul having said one word: 'Well did the Holy Spirit speak through Isaiah the prophet to our fathers, saying, "Go to this people and say: Hearing you shall hear and not understand; and seeing you shall see and not perceive. For the heart of this people has grown dull, and their ears are hard of hearing, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart, and should turn, and I should heal them." Be it known to you therefore that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will hear it.' And when he had said these things, the Jews departed, having much dispute among themselves. And he remained two whole years in his own hired lodging, and received all who came in to him, preaching the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all confidence, without hindrance. Here ends the Book of the Acts of the Apostles. Here begins the Prologue to the Canonical Epistles.

The order is not so among the Greeks, who, understanding fully and following the true faith, name the seven epistles canonical. As is found in the Latin codices, because Peter is first in the order of the apostles, his epistles are also first in order among the rest. But just as we have long since corrected the Gospels to the line of truth, so we render these also to their proper order, God assisting. For the first of them is that of James; two of Peter; three of John; and one of Jude. If these, as they were arranged by their authors, were also faithfully translated into Latin by the interpreters, they would not create ambiguity for readers, nor would the variety of wording conflict with itself—especially in that place where we read concerning the unity of the Trinity set forth in the first Epistle of John, in which we find that much error has been made by unfaithful translators…
